sheets.html:
An independent review of Carhartt Reworked for the D2C Recommerce & Site Merchandiser contract. I read all 3,545 published listings and 124 collections and found where one-of-a-kind inventory slips past the shopper: empty gift collections going into Q4, a fall season spelled two ways, the biggest sizes hidden behind “See More,” and schema that calls used gear new. Ten findings, four working fixes.

Read the findings →Try the fixes

Scope public storefront + Shopify's public product feed Checked 23 product pages Logins none

Condition report · fixed

Slightly
Worn

Size TALL L

Tag SM: fall-layers

Schema UsedCondition

Price ≤ new, by grade

10findings 3,545 published listings read, plus 124 collections

40.8% of them have nothing left to buy

0 products in six live gift collections, nine weeks before Black Friday

2 spellings of the fall-layers tag: 1,260 + 1,040, no overlap

23/23 product pages sampled that tell Google used gear is new

Why this store

Why
Carhartt Reworked

The posting doesn't name the client. Here's how I read it, and why I did this review before applying.

The posting saysWhat matches

Dearborn, MI Carhartt's headquarters is in Dearborn.

D2C Recommerce Carhartt Reworked is Carhartt's own resale store: used and repaired Carhartt gear, sold direct at reworked.carhartt.com.

Apparel, retail or consumer products Workwear and apparel.

Shopify Plus Reworked runs on Shopify. Its store ID is carhartt-trove.myshopify.com.

Seasonal merchandising · search & filters · product setup & QA The same jobs the ten findings below are sorted into.

Put together, the clues point to one store, so I did the job on it first. It's my read of a public posting, not inside information. If the client turns out to be another brand, the method carries over to any Shopify resale store: the same public feed, the same checks, the same tools.

Two reviews, one brand

In September I applied to Carhartt's Digital Site Merchandiser role and reviewed carhartt.com for it: 13 findings with working prototypes. This review covers Reworked. Together they cover Carhartt's main store and its resale store.

carhartt.com review ↗ Reworked findings ↓

Findings · 10 work orders

Where the gear
goes missing

Grouped by the four jobs in the posting. Each one has what I saw on September 25, why it costs sales, and what I'd ship first. Counts come from the store's own public product feed; screenshots are the storefront as a shopper sees it.

01 Work order
WO-01

Seasonal merchandising

Six gift collections are live — and empty

What I saw

Gifts for Him, Gifts for Her, Gifts Under $50 / $75 / $100 and Gifts for All are published with 0 products (last updated Jul 8, 2026). Meanwhile 429 in-stock listings still carry SM: Gifts — 297 men's, 172 women's.

Why it costs

Q4 is the biggest gifting window of the year, and gift pages are what email, paid social and the nav link to. An empty page there is a dead end at the worst possible time.

What I'd ship

Re-point the six rules to the gift tags with two guards: in stock only, and price within the band — 66 options tagged Gifts-50 are priced over $50. The builder below fills all six from today's catalog.

02 Work order
WO-02

Seasonal merchandising

St. Patrick's Day is still on the shelf — and so is a test

What I saw

“St. Patricks Day” (276 items) and “Shirt Jacs Test” (2,089 items) both render to shoppers and are listed in sitemap_collections_1.xml. A collection named test is published too.

Why it costs

Search engines and shoppers land on off-season and internal pages with the Carhartt name at the top, and they compete with the Fall Layers push for the same gear.

What I'd ship

301 St. Patrick's Day to Layers and the test copy to Shirt Jacs & Work Shirts, unpublish test, and add “retire last season” as a step in the pre-season checklist.

03 Work order
WO-03

Seasonal merchandising

Last season's campaign tags never came off

What I saw

1,013 listings are still tagged SM: sale-june-2026 (825 in stock). Cyber Monday 2025 exists in three spellings — SM: CyberMonday2025 947 · SM: CyberMonday-2025 583 · SM:CyberMonday 268 — beside SM: BFCM-2025 366 and SM: dec-26-2025-sale 927. 65 distinct SM: tags in all.

Why it costs

Every tag-driven collection, promo or report has to guess which spelling and which year it means. When Q4 2026 rules go live, last year's tags are still sitting on the same gear.

What I'd ship

One dated convention (SM: {event}-{yyyy}), a retire step on the campaign calendar, and a one-time cleanup map — the scanner below builds it from the live tags.

04 Work order
WO-04

Discoverability

Fall layers, spelled two ways

What I saw

The homepage leads with “Fall Layers With A Lot Of Life Left.” 2,300 listings carry a fall-layers tag: 1,260 as SM: Fall-layers and 1,040 as sm: fall-layers. Not one listing carries both.

Why it costs

Shopify's collection rules forgive case; exports, search-index boosts, feeds and BI filters often don't. Anything keyed to one spelling sees under 55% of the season's lead story.

What I'd ship

Pick one canonical tag and bulk-rewrite the other 1,040 in a single CSV pass, then lock the vocabulary so intake can't create a third.

05 Work order
WO-05

Discoverability

The Size filter hides the biggest sizes

What I saw

On Hoodies & Sweatshirts (734 items) the Size facet sorts alphabetically — 1X, 2X, 2XL, 2XL (TALL), 3X … 4XL (TALL), L — then stops at “See More.” M, S and XL, three of the four largest in-stock sizes (910 · 902 · 833 options), sit below the fold.

Why it costs

With one-of-a-kind stock, size is the first click. Every shopper in the most common sizes pays an extra click before the grid is useful.

What I'd ship

Sort sizes in size order (XS → 5XL, then Tall, then waist × inseam), open the facet by default on collection pages, and keep the ten most-stocked sizes above “See More.”

06 Work order
WO-06

Discoverability

TLL, XXL and 2XL — one size, three labels

What I saw

148 in-stock options say TLL instead of TALL (TLL L 71 · TLL 2XL 51 · TLL M 17). Women's 2XL appears as both XXL (108 in-stock options) and 2XL (58). Women's plus 1X/2X/3X sit beside men's 2XL/3XL with only “(REG)” to tell them apart. 281 distinct size labels are in stock.

Why it costs

A shopper who ticks “L (TALL)” never sees 71 tall larges. Split labels scatter the same size across checkboxes, and plus sizes read like typos.

What I'd ship

A size normalization map at intake, before listings reach Shopify (TLL → TALL, XXL → 2XL), and label women's plus as “2X (Women's Plus).” The facet fixer below shows before and after.

07 Work order
WO-07

Product setup & QA

A used short priced above new

What I saw

Relaxed 7″ Force Phoenix Pull On Short (style 106843): resale $35.00 – $59.00, and the same page shows New $44. The Slightly Worn L at $59 is in stock. Across the catalog, 7 size/condition options are priced above their own new price.

Why it costs

Resale sells on value. One visible price above new makes a shopper doubt every other price on the page.

What I'd ship

A price guard at listing — resale ≤ new × the grade's ceiling — plus a daily exception report of anything priced at or above new.

08 Work order
WO-08

Product setup & QA

Three in four listings show one stock photo

What I saw

2,611 of 3,545 listings (73.7%) have exactly one image, and 42 have none. All 20 in-stock PDPs I sampled caption it “Original product image; not actual item. Refer to the item's condition notes.” The median description is 53 characters; 391 are empty.

Why it costs

For used gear the photo and the condition note are the product. Someone buying “Slightly Worn” wants to see the wear before they commit.

What I'd ship

A condition-note template per grade and category, shown beside the price, and real-item photos first where the money is — outerwear, bibs and coveralls.

09 Work order
WO-09

Product setup & QA

Four in ten published listings have nothing to buy

What I saw

1,447 of 3,545 published listings (40.8%) are sold out in every size and condition. That includes 542 legacy listings with no Size or Condition option at all — none in stock. All 3,545 sit in the product sitemaps.

Why it costs

Sold-out one-of-a-kind pages soak up crawl budget, land search visitors on dead ends and pad internal search results.

What I'd ship

A sold-out policy: after N days with nothing to buy, unpublish or noindex and drop from the sitemap, with a 301 to the style's live listing or its collection.

10 Work order
WO-10

Search & feeds

Every product page tells Google the gear is new

What I saw

Product JSON-LD on 23 of 23 product pages sampled declares "itemCondition": "https://schema.org/NewCondition" — on listings sold as Like New, Slightly Worn and Broken In.

Why it costs

Google's merchant listing guidance expects UsedCondition for used goods. The mismatch risks Shopping disapprovals and tells every answer engine the wrong thing.

What I'd ship

Map the Condition option to UsedCondition with a short condition description in the theme's JSON-LD — about ten lines of Liquid, patch below.

Fixes · 4 working prototypes

Built on
today's catalog

Each tool runs on a snapshot of the store's public product feed from September 25 — 3,545 listings, 66 tags, 281 in-stock size labels. Nothing here touches the live store. It shows what the fix looks like before anyone changes a rule.

Fix 04 · for WO-10

UsedCondition schema patch

About ten lines of Liquid for the theme's Product JSON-LD. Every Reworked item is pre-owned, so each offer says so, and the grade rides along in the offer description.

{%- comment -%}
  Reworked · condition-aware offers for the Product JSON-LD.
  Replaces the "offers" block in the theme's product schema snippet.
  Every Reworked item is pre-owned, so each offer is UsedCondition;
  the grade (Like New / Slightly Worn / Broken In) goes in the description.
{%- endcomment -%}
{%- assign cond_opt = product.options_by_name['Condition'] -%}
"offers": [
  {%- for variant in product.variants -%}
    {%- liquid
      assign grade = 'Pre-owned'
      if cond_opt
        assign i = cond_opt.position | minus: 1
        assign grade = variant.options[i]
      endif
    -%}
    {
      "@type": "Offer",
      "sku": {{ variant.sku | json }},
      "price": {{ variant.price | divided_by: 100.0 | json }},
      "priceCurrency": {{ cart.currency.iso_code | json }},
      "availability": "https://schema.org/{% if variant.available %}InStock{% else %}OutOfStock{% endif %}",
      "itemCondition": "https://schema.org/UsedCondition",
      "description": {{ 'Pre-owned · ' | append: grade | json }},
      "url": {{ request.origin | append: variant.url | json }}
    }{% unless forloop.last %},{% endunless %}
  {%- endfor -%}
]

Drop-in for the offers array. Uses the Condition option by name, so it survives option reordering, and falls back to “Pre-owned” on the 542 legacy listings that have no Condition option.

The first 90 days

Q4 first,
then the system

Ordered by the calendar: fix what shoppers hit during gifting season, then the intake and tagging habits that make every season easier, then the reporting that proves it worked.

Days 1 – 30

Before the gifting rush

  • Fill the six gift pages from the tags already on the catalog, with the in-stock and price guards. QA every nav, email and paid link that points at them.
  • 301 St. Patrick's Day and Shirt Jacs Test, unpublish test, and add “retire last season” to the pre-season checklist.
  • One fall-layers tag: rewrite the 1,040 lowercase listings in a single CSV pass.
  • Ship the UsedCondition patch through theme QA and watch Merchant Center diagnostics.

Days 31 – 60

Make one-of-a-kind findable

  • Size normalization map at intake with the operations partner: TLL → TALL, XXL → 2XL, women's plus labeled.
  • Size facet in size order, open by default on collection pages, most-stocked sizes above “See More.”
  • Build BFCM and Cyber Monday 2026 on dated tags from the campaign calendar, with last year's scheduled to come off.
  • Daily exception report: anything priced at or above new, no photo, or an empty condition note.

Days 61 – 90

Measure and hand over

  • Sold-out policy live: after N days with nothing to buy, noindex or unpublish and 301 to the style's live listing.
  • Weekly view of sell-through by grade and size, gift and seasonal collection conversion, and facet use.
  • Real-item photo pilot on outerwear, bibs and coveralls, measured against stock-photo listings.
  • A written playbook — tag vocabulary, pre- and post-season checklists, intake QA — so the fixes stay fixed.

About

Who's
doing the work

I'm Mousa Batarseh, a web and e-commerce specialist in Warren, Michigan — about 25 minutes from Dearborn. For seven years I've run storefronts end to end for retail and wholesale brands: Shopify and WordPress stores for two textile and apparel brands run in parallel, catalog migrations of 14,000+ SKUs with redirects intact, and seasonal and promotional campaign pages for a multi-location Michigan retailer, built with its marketing and merchandising teams.

This review is the job as I read it: keep one-of-a-kind inventory findable, keep the seasonal story current, and keep product data clean enough that search, feeds and reporting can trust it. In September I also reviewed carhartt.com's main digital shelf — 13 findings with working prototypes.

The posting asks forWhat I bring

4+ years in merchandising or retail Seven years merchandising retail and wholesale storefronts — collections, navigation, campaign pages, product data (2019 – present).

1+ year of e-commerce Seven years across Shopify, WooCommerce and WordPress.

Apparel, retail or consumer products Two textile and apparel storefronts at Universal Wholesale & United Textile, and a multi-location Michigan retailer.

Shopify Plus and merchandising platforms Three years on Shopify: Liquid, smart collections, bulk CSV edits, theme work. Plus-only tools like Flow and Launchpad I'd learn on your store.

Adobe Analytics, Looker or similar GA4, Search Console and Tag Manager, plus Excel and Sheets for exports. Adobe Analytics and Looker would be new tools; the retail metrics behind them aren't.

Resale experience a plus Not yet in a resale role. This review is my homework on how graded, one-of-a-kind stock behaves on a storefront.

Dearborn, MI or remote Warren, MI. On-site days are easy; remote works too.

sheets.html:
Bran Marketing is the outsourced marketing department for industrial manufacturers, manufacturers' reps and wholesaler-distributors, and it is hiring a Web Development & Technical SEO Lead to build the web side of that department. On getbran.com, /web-design-seo carries no JSON-LD, and only 5 of 22 sitemap pages carry any. All 6 team pages still hold Wix placeholder copy, and Marsh & Moore, the build Bran presents as a case study, has 0 of 36 pages with a meta description. None of that is a backlog problem, so the department should start with a build standard, not a backlog: what I'd fix in week one, a line card you can filter, and the 90-day standard I'd run.

Findings five plates

What I'd fix in week one

Plate 01 Own house

Team pages are still on template URLs

All 6 team pages contain the Wix sentence “This is placeholder text. To change this content, double-click on the element and click Change Content.” Four of the six slugs name a different person: /team/brian-chung renders Alicia Branham, /team/ashley-amerson renders Marcie Flatt. /team is titled “Team (List) | Bran Marketing”, has no H1 and links to none of the six. 0 of 6 have a meta description.

What I'd ship in week one Real-name slugs with 301s from the old ones, placeholder blocks removed, a description and Person schema per page, and links from /team.

  • getbran.com/teamtitle “Team (List)”, 0 H1, 0 team links
  • /team/brian-chungrenders Alicia Branham
  • /team/ashley-amersonrenders Marcie Flatt

Plate 02 Coverage

The selling pages are silent

5 of 22 sitemap pages carry any JSON-LD: the homepage, /manufacturers, /the-bran-method, /marketing-consulting-training and /marshmoorecasestudy. The service and audience pages carry none: /web-design-seo, /manufacturers-reps, /wholesalers-distributors, /small-businesses, /the-bran-marketing-department, /3d-modeling-product-visualization. The blog is the exception: 15 of 15 sampled posts have BlogPosting, 4 with HowTo.

What I'd ship in week one One Service + BreadcrumbList block on every service and audience page, Organization declared once, the homepage graph deduplicated (WebSite appears twice).

  • getbran.com/web-design-seo0 JSON-LD blocks
  • /manufacturers-reps0 JSON-LD blocks
  • /wholesalers-distributors0 JSON-LD blocks

Plate 03 Signals

One post at three URLs, a members area in the sitemap

One post is live at three self-canonical URLs with the same title and H1: …-a-comprehensive-guide, …-a-comprehensive-guide-1 and /post/top-social-media-for-your-business. Every sampled post has two H1s (“BRANBLOG BY BRAN MARKETING” plus the title); 34 of 56 posts share the lastmod 2026-08-07. /groups, /forum and /members (H1 “BRAN MEMBER ONLY AREA”) are indexable and in the pages sitemap. llms.txt is present; /about-1 is a clean 404 with no internal links.

What I'd ship in week one One canonical URL for the post with 301s from the other two, one H1 in the blog template, noindex on the community pages, and a title lint: 12 of 47 titles pass 60 characters, the homepage's is 83.

  • getbran.com/post/top-social-media-for-your-businessthird copy, self-canonical
  • /members200, indexable, in sitemap
  • /llms.txt200, text/plain

Plate 04 Clients

Marsh & Moore: the case-study build has no meta layer

marshmoore.com (WordPress, Divi v.4.27.4) is the build Bran presents at /marshmoorecasestudy. Across 36 sampled pages: 0 meta descriptions, 0 JSON-LD, 0 Open Graph tags, 285 of 403 images with empty alt (29.3% coverage). Leftovers are live and indexable: /lines-represented/ (H1 “Portfolio Grid” / “No Results Found”), /sample-mfg/, /awl_filter_gallery/manufacturers-duplicate/, /home/ duplicating /, /contactus/ beside /contact-us/. It is also the lightest site here: 216,964 bytes of HTML at the median, 51 script tags, 0.52 s TTFB.

What I'd ship in week one Description, Open Graph and Organization + BreadcrumbList schema from one template hook, an alt-text pass, 301s or noindex for the leftovers, author archives out of the sitemap.

  • marshmoore.com0 description, 0 JSON-LD, 0 OG
  • /manufacturers/27 tiles, 28 of 32 images empty alt
  • getbran.com/marshmoore­casestudythe case study

Plate 05 Clients

Three line cards, none you can filter by what a buyer needs

Marsh & Moore's /manufacturers/: 27 logo tiles behind a Divi filter (All/Commercial/Residential/Waterworks/Irrigation), 28 of 32 images with empty alt, no PDF, a “Request Our Line Card!” form; 4 of 30 manufacturer pages unlinked from the grid. Tim Morales & Associates runs its line card through Wix Stores: 25 manufacturers behind a “Price $1–$250” slider, territory codes in slugs (-ms-la-al-wfl), /product-page/copy-of-franke-al-wfl rendering “Fluidmaster”. Armstrong-Weatherly's /line-card: title “2024 LINECARD”, H1 “2026 LINE CARD”, 13 manufacturers, 1 PDF, no filter or search, 8 of 21 manufacturer pages missing from it, 12 “I'm a product” placeholders in the sitemap since 2016-06-10.

What I'd ship in week one The prototype below: a line card with the facets a buyer uses, a spec sheet per product, and Product + DigitalDocument schema, on WordPress or Wix.

  • marshmoore.com/manufacturers/Divi filter, no PDF
  • timmorales.com/partnersWix Stores, price slider
  • armstrong-weatherly.com/line-card1 PDF, no filter

Method

166 read-only GET requests on 2026-09-22 between 13:23:32Z and 13:36:55Z, Chrome user agent, at least 0.6 s apart: robots.txt and every sitemap for all four sites, then 47 getbran.com pages plus llms.txt, 36 on marshmoore.com, 25 on timmorales.com, 30 on armstrong-weatherly.com. HTML bytes are the decoded body; TTFB is the final hop from an AWS host, so location-dependent. No Lighthouse or Core Web Vitals scores: PageSpeed Insights answered HTTP 429 for all four homepages.

Sec. 02 Prototype

A line card you can filter.

Three of the four sites publish a line card. None lets a buyer narrow it by size, material or lead time, and none marks up a spec sheet as structured data. This is the page type Bran's clients need most, built here as a static prototype: 18 fictional products from 6 fictional manufacturers, facets, search, a spec table per product, and Product + DigitalDocument JSON-LD that rewrites itself as you click. Everything in the demo is invented; no real Bran client products appear.

Ships on

The same standard on WordPress or Wix

Same fields, same facet names, same JSON-LD shape on either platform. That shared shape is the build standard.

WordPress

Custom post type + taxonomies
  • Content model a product post type; taxonomies for manufacturer, category, size range, material and lead time; specs as post meta; the spec sheet as an attachment on the product.
  • Facets FacetWP or a custom WP_Query with tax_query behind this same checkbox UI, filter state in the query string so a filtered view is shareable.
  • URLs /line-card/{category}/{product}/ via rewrite rules; manufacturer and category archives become landing pages.
  • Schema one wp_head hook builds Product, DigitalDocument, Offer and BreadcrumbList from post meta, so no editor touches code.
  • Performance server-rendered list, page cache, lazy images; only the facet script ships.

Wix

CMS collection + dataset filters
  • Content model a Products collection with reference fields to Manufacturers and Categories, tags for size range and material, a Document field for the PDF.
  • Facets a dynamic list page with dataset filters, or Velo wixData.query().hasSome() behind this checkbox UI; Wix Search for the text box.
  • URLs dynamic item pages at /line-card/{slug}; category pages from the Categories collection, picked up by the sitemap automatically.
  • Schema structured-data variables in the dynamic page's SEO settings, or wixSeo.setStructuredData() in Velo for the Product + DigitalDocument graph.
  • Performance the platform already ships 61 to 63 script tags per page at the median across the three Wix sites sampled, so keep sections and apps per page lean.

Sec. 03 Plan

Ninety days: a standard first, then the first build under it.

The findings above are not a backlog to grind through. They are what a build standard prevents: template leftovers, pages without schema, line cards that can't be filtered. So the department starts by writing the standard, uses the own-house fixes as its first test, then ships one client build the same way.

  1. Days 1–30

    Audit and baseline

    • Access: Search Console, GA4, Wix and WordPress admin, DNS. One URL inventory from robots.txt and every sitemap, this page's method made repeatable.
    • Baseline by page type: schema coverage, title and description lengths, H1 count, HTML weight, script count, TTFB; Lighthouse and CrUX when quota allows.
    • Own-house fixes: team slugs and placeholder copy, one canonical URL for the triple post, Service + BreadcrumbList on all 22 sitemap pages, noindex on /groups, /forum and /members, one H1 per post.
    • Deliverable: a one-page before/after in the same numbers as this review.

  2. Days 31–60

    Build standard

    • Templates for line card, manufacturer page and product/spec-sheet page on WordPress and Wix, with this prototype's facet UI.
    • Schema library: Organization, Service, BreadcrumbList, Product, DigitalDocument, Offer, BlogPosting, Person, validated in QA.
    • Migration checklist: URL inventory, redirect map, 404 sweep, alt text, metadata, sitemap and robots, launch QA.
    • Performance budget per template and a launch checklist: viewport, canonical, one H1, description, schema, alt coverage.
    • Estimating and time-tracking template so web work fits inside client credits and account leads see where hours go.

  3. Days 61–90

    First build under the standard

    • One client build or migration end to end: scope, estimate, build, QA, launch, redirects verified in Search Console.
    • Process documented where the team works: templates, checklists, handoff notes, a written definition of done.
    • Handoff: designers and account managers can brief web work without a developer in the room.
    • Retro against the posting's criteria, with numbers; the standard revised from what the build taught.

How the posting says I'd be measured, and what I'd show

Technical performance
The baseline numbers move: own-house schema coverage from 5 of 22 pages to all 22, team pages off template slugs, weight tracked per template.
Communication
A one-page weekly note: what shipped, what's blocked, what it cost in hours. Findings written like this page, evidence first.
Reliability
Hours tracked against estimates, dates kept, redirects checked in Search Console after every launch.
Team fit
A small team where design leads the work: I build what the designers design, brief in plain language, and say what's hard before it's late.

Sec. 04 About

Said plainly: what I bring.

  1. Seven years of web development, WordPress since 2019. Independent contractor: I scope, estimate, track hours and ship.
  2. A production Wix build for K-WAV (now Total LED), a Direct-View LED display manufacturer: spec-sheet product-line pages, forms, and rebrand-migration planning. k-wav.com
  3. 14,000+ SKU catalog migrations at Universal Wholesale / United Textile, with redirects, data cleanup and QA. mousabatarseh.com/changeatlasmousabatarseh.com/SEO-Tools
  4. Schema/JSON-LD and Core Web Vitals into the high 90s. Two more reviews in this format: mousabatarseh.com/salt-reviewmousabatarseh.com/oakwood-review

End of review

sheets.html:
Sec. 01 — Overview · for the DTC Ecommerce Ops & Insights Specialist role

Evidence page · sampled 2026-09-20

PetSafe already runs the toolchain the job description asks about — Gatsby on Netlify, headless Shopify, Sanity, Klaviyo, Algolia, Triple Whale, GTM, Bazaarvoice — I can see every one of them loading on petsafe.com. What's missing is the plumbing that turns that stack into trustworthy data and repeatable launches: zero structured data on the homepage, a sitemap URL that serves HTML instead of XML, no llms.txt, and every product page shipping the same 15-word templated meta description. Every figure below is dated and reproducible.

0 application/ld+json blocks on the petsafe.com homepage

2026-09-20 23:20 UTC · curl petsafe.com/ | grep -c 'application/ld+json' → 0 in 428,751 bytes · [E1]

HTML

/sitemap.xml returns the Gatsby homepage HTML, not an XML sitemap

2026-09-20 23:20 UTC · curl petsafe.com/sitemap.xml → 360,985 bytes, first 500 chars begin <!DOCTYPE html> · [E2]

404 /llms.txt — missing AI-ingestion signal

2026-09-20 23:20 UTC · curl -I petsafe.com/llms.txt → HTTP/2 404 · [E3]

15 Words in the meta description on every product page — the same template, verbatim

2026-09-20 23:20 UTC · 5 product pages sampled; each returns "Buy the [name] in the official PetSafe® store for your pet." · [E4]

Signals

Structured data is silent on the front door

Homepage carries no JSON-LD; interior product pages carry ProductGroup, BreadcrumbList and hand-curated FAQPage. The gap is only at the top of the funnel.

2026-09-20 · homepage grep returned 0; product page /p/extreme-weather-aluminum-pet-door/ZPA19-16853/ returned 2 JSON-LD blocks (Product+Breadcrumb, FAQPage) · [E5]

Operations

Sitemap and llms.txt need owners

curl https://www.petsafe.com/sitemap.xml returns 200 with Content-Type: text/html. A specialist who owns URL taxonomy owns this — the fix is one build-time step.

2026-09-20 · see [E2] and [E3]

Insights

The stack for Tableau is already emitting events

GTM is live, Klaviyo is firing, Shopify is behind the cart, Triple Whale is watching spend, Bazaarvoice is collecting reviews. Tableau dashboards described in the JD can be built on top of what's already flowing, not from scratch.

2026-09-20 · HTML-source grep on the homepage — see stack node counts on the next page and [E6]

What I looked at

About 90 minutes with public artifacts only — the pages, HTTP headers, robots.txt, sitemap and llms.txt endpoints, the JSON-LD on 5 real product pages across doors, GPS, and microchip categories, and the raw HTML of petsafe.com/. No login, no confidential data. Every claim on this site names a reproducible source; the Evidence Log at the bottom of this page shows the exact commands.

Role fit

The JD splits the role into four buckets: project management, data & Tableau, Shopify ops, and measurement. This review walks through one artifact — the DTC storefront — in those four voices, plus a fifth section (The 1,000-Page Fix) with a live interactive tool that repairs a specific problem I found on every product page. I've been the "keep it moving" person for a 14,000-SKU Shopify migration at Universal Wholesale and I run this same pattern across storefronts today.

Scope petsafe.com · homepage + 5 product pages Method curl, page source, robots, sitemap, llms.txt, JSON-LD parse Stack seen Gatsby 5.16.1 / Netlify / Shopify / Sanity / Klaviyo / Algolia / Triple Whale / Bazaarvoice / GTM Independent — not affiliated with PetSafe Brands

Evidence log

Every claim on this page, with its date, source, and a command you can rerun.

Same 5 URLs on 2026-09-20 23:22 UTC each returned 2 JSON-LD blocks: block 0 is a @graph containing a ProductGroup with variants; block 1 is a @graph containing a BreadcrumbList and a hand-curated FAQPage. The ProductGroup.description field is 1,914–3,626 characters on the products I sampled.
  6. [E6] Stack fingerprints in petsafe.com/ HTML source, sampled 2026-09-20 23:20 UTC. Case-insensitive grep counts: cdn.shopify.com = 12; sanity = 149; klaviyo = 4; algolia = 3; triplewhale = 5; bazaarvoice = 5; gtm.js = 2. generator meta tag reads Gatsby 5.16.1; response headers include server: Netlify.

Sec. 02 — Stack & Data Loop · GA4 · Shopify · Tableau

Half evidence · half prescription — each block below is labeled

A DTC Ops & Insights Specialist inherits, not builds from scratch. Before proposing dashboards, it's worth counting what's already emitting events. Numbers below are grep counts against the raw HTML of petsafe.com/ sampled 2026-09-20 23:20 UTC — reproducible one-liners in the evidence log at the bottom.

Frontend

Gatsby 5.16.1 Netlify-hosted static frontend. generator meta tag public. React Helmet drives per-page meta. 2026-09-20 · <meta name="generator" content="Gatsby 5.16.1">; response server: Netlify

CMS

Sanity

149 references in home HTML. Content model likely feeds every brand under one repo. 2026-09-20 · grep -oiE 'sanity' home.html | wc -l → 149

Commerce

Headless Shopify

Cart and checkout run on Shopify behind the Gatsby shell. 2026-09-20 · grep -oiE 'cdn\.shopify\.com' home.html | wc -l → 12; also confirmed by /cart.json disallow in robots.txt

Email & SMS

Klaviyo

4 refs in HTML. /klaviyo-form/ disallowed in robots — form endpoints are template routes. 2026-09-20 · grep -oiE 'klaviyo' home.html | wc -l → 4

Search

Algolia

3 refs. Powers on-site search. Ties directly to conversion funnel measurement. 2026-09-20 · grep -oiE 'algolia' home.html | wc -l → 3

Attribution

Triple Whale

5 refs. Cross-channel attribution and pixel — checks the box on the JD's preferred list. 2026-09-20 · grep -oiE 'triplewhale' home.html | wc -l → 5

Reviews

Bazaarvoice

5 refs. Product ratings + Q&A widgets. Robots blocks ?bvstate= parameters (good). Reviews widget has data-bv-seo="false" — reviews aren't SEO-rendered. Fix on Sec. 05. 2026-09-20 · attr grep on a real product page

Tag Manager

GTM

gtm.js loads. This is the injection point for a clean, documented event layer. 2026-09-20 · grep -oiE 'gtm\.js' home.html | wc -l → 2

The data loop I'd trust

Prescription · what I would build once hired

The JD asks for "trusted Tableau dashboards and consistent definitions for core DTC performance." Trust is built at the seams, not in the dashboard. Here's the loop I'd defend:

# The four seams that most often desync
Shopify order  ─▶  GA4 purchase       # dedupe on order_id, not transaction_id
GA4 session    ─▶  Triple Whale       # UTM taxonomy is the join key
Klaviyo event  ─▶  GA4 event          # email_opened ≠ engagement — define once
Algolia click  ─▶  GA4 view_item      # tie internal-search results to conversion
# Then Tableau reads from one place — a modeled layer, not raw connectors
Modeled layer  ─▶  Tableau           # definitions live in a shared metric dictionary

Definition first

Metric dictionary before any new dashboard

"Conversion rate," "AOV," "new vs. returning" — each defined with the exact filter, window, and source of truth. One page, versioned, linked from every dashboard.

Reconciliation, weekly

Shopify ↔ GA4 ↔ Triple Whale

A one-tab Tableau view that flags any day where the three sources disagree on order count by >3%. Silent 99% of the time; loud when something's actually broken.

AI in the loop, not on the throne

Claude for exploration, humans for calls

The JD is explicit — approved AI tools "explore data exports, identify patterns or anomalies" but outputs are validated. I already use Claude this way for weekly SKU-health and search-console rollups.

The three gaps at the front door

Evidence · sampled 2026-09-20

Front-door signal quality

  • Homepage schema. Zero application/ld+json blocks on petsafe.com/. Recommend Organization + WebSite + BreadcrumbList as the baseline; brand-page schema per sub-brand. 2026-09-20 · [E1] on Overview SEO · owner

sheets.title: Every promo is a runway, not a launch.
sheets.html:
Sec. 03 — Campaign Runway · intake → QA → launch → readout

Prescription · this is what I would build; the worked SportDOG example below is hypothetical

The JD's operator-voice sentence is my favorite line in the whole post: "Shopify changes, campaigns, promotions, and site initiatives launch accurately and on time, with strong pre- and post-launch QA." That's the outcome I'd sign up to be measured on. Here's how I'd get there — a single template that scales across brands, one shared UTM taxonomy, one QA gate.

Intake template — one page, one form

Marketing, merch, and brand shouldn't have to know how the sausage is made. They fill out this form; I make it real.

# campaign-brief.md — filed in the ops backlog on submit
brand:            PetSafe | SportDOG | Invisible Fence | ScoopFree | ...
campaign_name:    SportDOG SD-425X Fall Hunt Promo
offer:            $40 off, code HUNT40, min $199
skus_in_scope:    SD-425X, SD-1225X, SD-1825X (3 SKUs, 1 collection)
go_live:          2026-10-01 06:00 America/New_York
end:              2026-10-14 23:59 America/New_York
channels:         Klaviyo email, on-site banner, paid social, organic social
success_metric:   Incremental units on the 3 SKUs vs. prior-4-week baseline
approver:         CRM lead + brand owner (JD boundary rule)

UTM taxonomy — one page, hard rules

The single most common cause of "the numbers don't agree" is inconsistent UTMs. This is the rule sheet I'd publish and enforce.

# All lowercase. No spaces. No punctuation. Hyphens only.
utm_source    = the platform: klaviyo | meta | google | tiktok | pinterest | affiliate-{name}
utm_medium    = the channel type: email | sms | paid-social | paid-search | organic-social | display
utm_campaign  = {brand}-{offer-slug}-{yyyy-mm}   e.g. sportdog-hunt40-2026-10
utm_content   = the creative: {format}-{variant}  e.g. hero-a | carousel-v2 | button-primary
utm_term      = paid only: keyword or audience id
# Bonus: a 'sub_id' cookie captured at first-touch for later attribution reconciliation.

Why this matters for Tableau

utm_campaign is the join key across Klaviyo, Triple Whale, GA4, and Shopify. If it's inconsistent, every dashboard downstream lies quietly. The rule above is boring on purpose.

Pre-launch QA — the 20-line gate

Nothing goes live until every box is checked. I ran a version of this for United Textile Wholesale's Shopify migration; the shape is the same regardless of stack.

Pre-launch QA — SportDOG SD-425X Fall Hunt Promo (worked example)

  • Discount code HUNT40 created, $ off, min $199, correct SKUs, correct dates (Shopify admin)Shopify
  • Collection page shows the 3 SKUs, correct order, correct pricing, no orphaned productsShopify
  • Product page copy & images updated in Sanity, published to preview URL, brand-owner approval loggedSanity
  • Homepage banner links to the collection with correct UTMs (per taxonomy sheet)Sanity + UTM
  • Klaviyo send list segmented, subject line + preview text spellchecked, links carry correct UTMsKlaviyo
  • Paid social creative delivered to media buyer with the exact UTM string, not a BitlyPaid
  • GA4 event for select_promotion firing on the banner (checked in DebugView)GA4
  • Triple Whale campaign named to match utm_campaign exactlyTriple Whale
  • Tableau: baseline snapshot for the 3 SKUs (prior 4 weeks) exported and pinnedTableau
  • Bazaarvoice widget still loading on the 3 PDPs; no missing reviews behind the discountBazaarvoice
  • Rollback plan written: 3 steps, 5 minutes, doesn't require a developerOps
  • All of the above logged in the campaign brief; brief timestamped and posted in the channelPM

Post-launch — day 1, day 7, close

Day 1 · monitoring

15 minutes at go-live, then a check at hour 2 and hour 6

Look at three numbers: sessions to the collection, code applications, orders. If any is zero when it shouldn't be, walk the funnel with the UTM.

Day 7 · early read

Half-page readout in the channel, in prose, not a dashboard link

What ran, what converted, one thing that surprised us, one thing to change in the second week. Written so a busy CRM lead reads it in 60 seconds.

Close · learnings

One row in the promo library, one paragraph, versioned

Over a year, this library becomes the answer to "have we tried something like this before?" — which is the question that most often blocks a decision.

The pattern is portable

I've run the intake → QA → launch → close loop for seasonal apparel drops at United Textile Wholesale and for multi-location retail at Wild Bill's Tobacco. The names on the columns change; the shape doesn't.

Worked example hypothetical SportDOG fall promo Real evidence Klaviyo, Sanity, Bazaarvoice live on petsafe.com Rollout one brand first, then the family

Sec. 04 — First 30 / 60 / 90 · what I'd close, ship, and give back

Prescription · forward-looking plan; resume evidence at the bottom

The success criteria in the posting end with this: "Channel owners regain measurable capacity for strategy because technical coordination, detailed execution, and analysis are handled." That's the single sentence I optimize for. Here's how I'd spend the first 90 days making that line real — grounded in what I already saw on petsafe.com, sized to a specialist role, and honest about what I would not touch.

Window What I ship How it maps to the JD Status
Days 1–14
Listen		 Shadow one launch end to end (whichever brand is next). Read every existing Tableau workbook and note what's trusted, what's stale, what nobody looks at. Meet the CRM, SEO, brand, and dev leads. Read the roadmap. Ask questions, don't propose. PM & ops; measurement plans; the boundary rules from the JD (channel owners keep strategy). Now
Days 15–30
Close the front-door tickets		 Homepage JSON-LD (Organization + WebSite + BreadcrumbList). Fix /sitemap.xml so it serves XML. Publish a /llms.txt. Ship a UTM taxonomy sheet and get sign-off. Baseline the "elbow grease" backlog into a single tracker. "Elbow grease" cleanup; UTM discipline; documentation; SOPs; the "trusted definitions" prerequisite. Now
Days 31–60
One trusted dashboard		 Stand up (or refactor) one Tableau workbook that reconciles Shopify ↔ GA4 ↔ Triple Whale daily, with a red flag when they disagree >3%. Publish the metric dictionary next to it. Ship the campaign brief template + pre-launch QA gate as a working artifact. Run one AI-assisted anomaly scan per week and validate the outputs. Tableau; GA4; Triple Whale; approved AI usage (Claude/ChatGPT with validation); campaign QA.
Days 61–90
Give capacity back		 Absorb the recurring "coordinate this promo" work from the CRM and SEO leads so they get their afternoons back. Own end-to-end delivery of 2 campaigns from intake to close, with post-launch readouts in prose. Start a prioritized experimentation backlog with hypothesis + measurement plan for each item. The capacity line. Recurring readouts. Experimentation. All measurable. Later

What I would not do

Boundary

Not touch strategy or brand direction

Those stay with channel owners. My job is execution, coordination, and honest reporting on what shipped.

Boundary

Not try to be a data scientist

The JD is clear that this isn't a modeling role. AI helps me summarize and spot anomalies; humans validate; big questions escalate.

Boundary

Not turn the site into a science project

Every ticket has a business reason and an owner. If it doesn't, it doesn't get pulled.

Why I already fit

A short pattern-match from my resume to the four JD buckets — no fluff.

JD bucketEvidence from my work
Technical PM & ops Led Universal Wholesale's migration from a legacy HTML catalog to a B2B ordering platform: 14,000+ product records prepared, validated, and imported with repeatable cleanup / exception-tracking / QA processes. Owned intake through launch.
Data analysis & Tableau-adjacent GA4 + Search Console are my daily view for reporting today. I run weekly rollups with Claude and ChatGPT to spot anomalies (with validation) and build my own catalog QA tools — one is CSV Mapper, live at mousabatarseh.com/csv-mapper.
DTC & Shopify ops Three years on Shopify — currently the United Textile Wholesale storefront (Ferndale, MI), previously as part of Universal Wholesale's platform work. Collections, coupons, seasonal promo calendars, pre-/post-launch QA, and the catalog data behind all of it.
Measurement, testing, continuous improvement Five years of on-page SEO and content ops, structured data, canonical / sitemap hygiene across my own domains (mousabatarseh.com and work.mousabatarseh.com — public PageSpeed & Search Console evidence available on request). Documented and versioned, not one-off.

One last thing

I built this microsite in one working session using the same Award Row design system I use for the rest of my portfolio. The whole review — HTML, CSS, evidence, checklists — is under 40KB, no build step, hosts on Netlify or Vercel as-is. If that pace is useful, I'd love to bring it to PetSafe.

sheets.html:
Sec. 05 — The 1,000-Page Fix · a specific problem, cited on 5 real product pages

Evidence + prescription — every claim on this page names the URL and the date I sampled it

Every PetSafe product page ships the same 15-word templated meta description:
"Buy the [product name] in the official PetSafe® store for your pet."
Meanwhile, the JSON-LD on the same page carries 1,500–3,600 characters of rich, benefit-focused product copy — copy that PetSafe already wrote, already stores in Sanity, already renders as machine-readable schema. That copy just never reaches <meta name="description">. Every product page's Google snippet, every social share preview, every AI answer citation, uses the template. Fix once in the Gatsby template. Ships every page.

5 / 5 Product pages sampled across doors, GPS, and microchip categories — all ship the identical templated meta description

2026-09-20 23:22 UTC · URLs and raw <meta> tags below · [F1]

15 Words in the current template — the same 15 words on every page, only the product name changes

2026-09-20 · template is "Buy the [name] in the official PetSafe® store for your pet."

2026-09-20 · len(JSON-LD.description) on /p/gps-dog-tracker-bundle/PTK00-18293/ · [F2]

1× Gatsby template change to fix every product page at once — the fix scales O(1), not O(N)

The Repair Bench

Pick a real PetSafe product below. Each column shows one option for the meta description on that page: what ships today, an automatic extract from the description already on the page, or a rewritten version hand-crafted to the 150-char sweet spot. The mock SERP result below the columns shows what Google would render for each. Every product's data on this page was pulled from the live URL on 2026-09-20 23:22 UTC.

Where in the stack this fix lives

Prescription · one field, one template line

# Sanity schema — the product document already has these fields
product {
  name:          string
  description:   portableText   # ← rich copy, already written, currently only feeds JSON-LD
  seoDescription: string, 155 max # ← ADD THIS. Optional; falls back to auto-extract from `description`.
  ...
}
# Gatsby template — one line change in the <Helmet> block
<meta
  name="description"
  content={
    product.seoDescription             # explicit override wins
    || firstSentence(product.description, 155)  # auto-extract fallback
    || `Buy the ${product.name} in the official PetSafe® store for your pet.` # current template stays as last resort
  }
/>

Ownership

This is the DTC Ops role, not a dev sprint

Sanity schema change: schema editor. Gatsby template change: one PR, one file, ~6 lines. Content: I write the first 20 seoDescription values for the top-selling products, and hand marketing/merch a template so they can write the rest at their own pace.

Measurement

Success is provable in Search Console

Baseline the top 20 product URLs' CTR and impressions this month. Ship the change. Read Search Console at 30 and 60 days. If the fix works, CTR on those URLs moves; if it doesn't, we know before we've scaled it.

Bonus finding

Bazaarvoice Reviews SEO is off

On the same product pages, the Questions widget carries data-bv-seo="true". The Reviews widget carries data-bv-seo="false". Reviews are the bigger data set and they're invisible to Google. Same category of fix; same order of magnitude of upside.

2026-09-20 · attribute grep on /p/extreme-weather-aluminum-pet-door/ZPA19-16853/

The line I keep coming back to

This fix ships once and improves every product URL PetSafe has. It uses copy PetSafe already paid to write. It doesn't touch strategy, brand voice, or roadmap priorities. It's exactly the shape of ticket the "elbow grease backlog" line in the JD was written about — and it's the kind of thing I'd pull off the shelf in my first 30 days.

A multi-state chain lives or dies on rollout readiness: one promo, one plan, every state version right on launch day and gone on take-down day. So I read highprofilecannabis.com the way a retail-marketing ops lead would: one campaign, seven state versions, three stores in one market — and marked each item the way a launch board would.

The board

HP-06Needs review

Store status and count disagree across surfaces

Manchester, CT: homepage grid says “Coming Soon”; the store selector on the same page says “Shop Now”; the store page shows hours and 312 live SKUs. Lexington, KY's shop links point to /stores/c3-industries-ky-sandbox (404). Store count: 35 in the site selector, “32 Locations” on c3industries.com, “31 operating stores across six states” on /retail/ — followed by a list of seven states. highprofilecannabis.com home · /ct/manchester/ · /lexington/ · c3industries.com · c3industries.com/retail/ · observed Sep 20, 2026C12 Store codesC14 Channel build

What's working

State compliance lines are present and correctly different per market — Michigan's Poison Control line, Missouri's “Medical decisions should not be made based on advertising”, Massachusetts' CCC language, New Jersey's licensing line. That's the hard part of multi-state promo copy, and it's done. Regular prices on the house brands are consistent across the three Missouri stores for 204 identical SKUs; the drift is in promo depth, which is a rollout decision, not a data error. And every Missouri product page server-renders its full price and special data, which is what made this review checkable at all.

Method & scope

Public pages only, Sep 20, 2026: the seven state deals pages, 35 location pages, sitemaps, c3industries.com, and product pages for St Louis, Chesterfield and Branson (Missouri) plus Kalamazoo, Webberville, Buchanan, Grand Rapids 44th, Dorchester and Manchester menus via the site's own menu endpoint. Specials carry no start/end dates in the menu data, so expiry on menus couldn't be checked — only the WordPress deals pages expose dates. Cross-state price differences (MA vs MO) are expected and not counted. I haven't checked a cart.

What I bring, plainly. Six years of promotion calendars, catalog pricing and campaign pages for two Michigan wholesalers, and the QA system this review runs on. I haven't bought out-of-home or print media; this review is about digital rollout readiness, and that's the work I'm asking to do.

sheets.html:
Nothing here needs a new tool. It needs one owner per date, one master block per campaign, and a check that runs per state version.

Week 1

Take down, fix, template

  • Replace the Labor Day hero on all seven state deals pages; archive the rules at a real URL
  • One master legal block with state slots (warning, eligibility, address) — CT date and KY rules fixed by construction
  • Rename shopper-facing specials that carry internal codes (“MO CF – …”)

Weeks 2–3

Rollout sheet + readiness grid

  • One row per promo per state: dates, take-down owner, stores, depth, legal block ID, CTA
  • Readiness grid (page 02) run at launch and at take-down
  • Market-level promo depth written into the rollout plan; exceptions named

Week 4

Weekly escalation & KPI

  • Weekly promo report: live vs planned, expired-still-live, per-state copy drift
  • Store-launch checklist: status on all three surfaces, meta, LocalBusiness schema, menu slug
  • Store count reconciled across highprofilecannabis.com and c3industries.com

What I'd want to know first

Who owns the WordPress deals pages versus the menu specials — they're two systems and the expiry problem lives in the gap. Whether Missouri promo depth is set per store on purpose (a new store, aged stock) or rolled out once and edited locally. Which legal copy each state's compliance team has already approved, so the master block starts from their text, not mine. And I'd want the out-of-home and print calendar in the same sheet — I haven't bought that media, but I can make sure it launches on the same dates as the web version.

sheets.title: Top-shelf menus, running on store data that disagrees with itself.
sheets.html:
Catalog · deals · store data

JARS runs 55 stores across Michigan, Arizona and Colorado on one storefront. I read it the way a revenue-strategy team would want it read: the deals attached to real products, the store records behind every location page, and the data search engines are handed about both. Six findings; each maps to a check in the promotion QA engine I built.

55 store records
MI 34 · AZ 19 · CO 2

10,532 active deal records read

25 products with two prices for the same bundle (Lansing + Ann Arbor)

3 stores whose page and schema list different phone numbers

13 Arizona pages with an unfilled map template

Findings

What a catalog check would have stopped

1Blocked

Two prices for the same seven-cart bundle

At Lansing, 14 products carry both 7/$80 Cartridges 2g and 7/$90 Cartridges 2g at once; at Ann Arbor, 11 (Mitten Extracts “Super Nurdz”, “Rainbow Sherbert”, “Blueberry Pie” cartridges among them). Same quantity, two totals, one product. The pair 7/$60 and 7/$69 repeats the pattern.

POST /api/v1/product-service/filter (Lansing 1,557 SKUs, Ann Arbor 1,154) · /deals · observed Sep 20, 2026

C11 ConflictC5 Price math

2Needs review

A volume ladder where buying more costs more

2/$25 Pods 1g ($12.50 each) and 3/$40 Pods 1g ($13.33 each) are attached to the same STIIIZY pods at Flint, East Detroit, Hazel Park, Lansing and Ann Arbor; Wana gummies carry the same 2/$25 vs 3/$40 pair. The bigger bundle has the higher unit price.

Same menu endpoint, five Michigan stores · observed Sep 20, 2026

C5 Price mathC6 Cap

3Blocked

The homepage lists Poison Control as customer service

Homepage Organization schema: contactPoint.telephone: +1-800-222-1222, contactType: "Customer Service". That's the National Poison Control hotline — correctly used in the footer warning, then reused as the company's phone for search engines. The same block lists 35 stores and none of the 19 in Arizona.

jarscannabis.com homepage JSON-LD · observed Sep 20, 2026

C16 WordingC12 Store codes

4Blocked

Store phone numbers that differ on the same page

Grand Rapids 40th St: schema +1-616-931-9900, page (616) 931-0990 — transposed. Mt Morris: schema 810-225-3300, page (810)-255-3300. South Phoenix: schema +16024910420, page (602) 900-1867. Seven different phone formats across the 55 store records.

/mi/grand-rapids-40th-st · /mi/mt-morris · /az/south-phoenix-dispensary · observed Sep 20, 2026

C12 Store codes

5Needs review

Thirteen Arizona pages ship an unfilled template

Store schema sameAs Apple Maps link contains auid=PUT_ACTUAL_AUID_HERE on 13 Arizona location pages (Mesa among them). Four Michigan pages (Okemos, Owosso, Oxford, River Rouge) have no store schema at all. El Mirage's hours are literally "start":"open","end":"open" all week.

/az/mesa and 12 others · /mi/okemos · /az/el-mirage · observed Sep 20, 2026

C1 RequiredC15 Assets

6Needs review

45% of active deals end in the year 4200

Of 10,532 active deal records, 4,768 carry endStamp: 4200-04-19 — a far-future date standing in for “no end”. One active “4 for $20 Keef Cola” deal (start 2023-06-01) is attached to a store that exists only in the closed-store list, which redirects to /find-a-dispensary. 108 deal names appear twice at the same store with the same URL slug.

GET /api/v1/deals · retailer-settings-cms/closed-retailer-routes · observed Sep 20, 2026

C10 DatesC12 Store codes

What's working

The hard parts are already built

One storefront serves 55 stores, three states and two menu types from a single Dutchie-fed catalog with loyalty wired in — the plumbing most chains never finish. Every Michigan page carries the full CRA-style footer warning. Menu data is structured and consistent enough that every finding above came from a query, not a guess. The problems are in the records going in, which is the cheapest place to fix them.

Method & scope

Public data only, Sep 20, 2026: 55 location pages and their JSON-LD, the homepage schema, sitemaps (11,337 product URLs), and the unauthenticated storefront endpoints the site itself calls — all store records, the chain-wide deals feed (10,532 rows) and full menus for Lansing, Ann Arbor, Flint, East Detroit and Hazel Park. I didn't render /deals in a browser, so whether the storefront hides one of two conflicting deals isn't confirmed; the conflict is in the data it loads. Whether the 4200 end date is a Dutchie convention or a JARS entry practice is unknown. I haven't worked in cannabis; I have run two wholesalers' catalogs and promotion calendars.

Why this matters for revenue

Store name, phone, hours and address are what Google Maps, Apple Maps and every “dispensary near me” search show before anyone reaches the menu. sheets.html:
Plan · first 30 days

Nothing here needs a new platform; it needs rules at the point data goes in.

30 days

Week 1

Stop the wrong numbers

  • Replace 800-222-1222 in the homepage schema; add the 19 Arizona stores
  • Fix the three phone mismatches and El Mirage's hours
  • Retire one of each same-quantity deal pair (7/$80 vs 7/$90, 7/$60 vs 7/$69)

Weeks 2–3

Rules at intake

  • Deal sheet row requires a real end date or an explicit “evergreen” flag — no year-4200 stand-ins
  • Ladder check: each tier cheaper per unit than the one below
  • Store pages render schema from the store record; fill the 13 map IDs

Week 4

Weekly report

  • Deals submitted, cleared first pass, blocked, and which check fired
  • Store-record drift: any page whose phone, hours or city differs from the record
  • Orphan deals attached to closed stores, and duplicate deal slugs

What I'd ask first

Whether the storefront already suppresses one of two conflicting deals at checkout (that changes finding 1 from a pricing problem to a display one). Who owns deal entry — Dutchie at the store, or a central team — because the ladder rule belongs wherever the deal is typed. And whether the 4200 end date is a platform default or a habit; one is a setting, the other is a checklist line.

sheets.title: What the deal says, and what the rule does
sheets.html:
Promotion rollout review · lume.com

Six findings from reading lume.com's specials the way a rollout coordinator would: deal by deal, store by store, against the numbers the site itself serves.

Tab 1 · Findings Observed Sep 20, 2026
Ann Arbor store selected

Promotions only work if they reach every store the way they were planned: right price, right dates, right stores, right disclaimer. So I read lume.com the way a promotions coordinator would — deal by deal, store by store — and checked whether what the site promises is what the rules actually do. Six things a rollout checklist would have caught, each with the check that catches it.

Menu SKUs readActive discountsBundle prices above the single priceStore pages with conflicting hours
888 (Ann Arbor)117509 SKU-bundle pairs32 of 40

Findings

What the site promises vs. what the rules do

01

Two bundles, same ten jars, two prices — both worse than buying singles

Baller Jars 7g – 2/$80 (weekly, ends 09-29) and Baller Jars 7g – 2/$98 (ongoing, no end date) target the identical ten Cannalicious SKUs and are both displayed. Those jars are $60 regular and $39 each right now under Cannalicious & Detroit Edibles – 35% Off. So the “deal” prices — $40 and $49 a jar — are both higher than two singles ($78). Across the Ann Arbor menu I counted 509 SKU-bundle pairs where the bundle's per-unit price is above the item's current single sale price, and 157 SKUs sitting in two or more bundles.

Evidence: lume.com/specials/all (Ann Arbor) · discount ids 135314, 134549, 134849 · Ann Arbor menu, 888 SKUs · observed Sep 20, 2026

C11 ConflictC5 Price math

02

A daily deal named 20% Off is configured at 25%

Daily Deal – Lume 3.5g 20% Off (id 135412, Tuesdays) carries unitPercentOff: 0.25. Every other “20% Off” deal on the same page — Doobie Tuesday, Muha Mates 5Pk — is configured at 0.2. The name promises one number and the rule applies another. (Read from the page's own data payload; not verified in a Tuesday cart.)

Evidence: lume.com/specials/all · discountTypeMap · ids 135412, 135491 · observed Sep 20, 2026

C5 Price mathC16 Wording

03

The homepage “$15 Each” eighth lands on a $17.50-each bundle

Hero slides Lume 1/8th Ongoing Global (“$20 Each”) and Lume 1/8th Ongoing Outlet (“$15 Each”) both deep-link to /specials/bundles/135343 = Flower 3.5g – 2/$35, $17.50 each. At the seven outlet stores the same eighths are $15 single, so the call-to-action lands on a bundle that costs more than the advertised price. Mount Pleasant Broomfield is on both slides' store lists — it shows “$20 Each” and “$15 Each” for the same eighths at once.

Evidence: lume.com homepage hero data (content_filter_locations) · /specials/bundles/135343 · Ann Arbor menu · observed Sep 20, 2026

C12 Store scopeC15 Assets

04

A deal called “Disposable 2g” contains 1g carts

Disposable 2g – 2/$35 (id 135330) targets nine Mitten Extracts … Disposable Cart 1g SKUs ($18 reg). The sibling Disposable 2g – 2/$40 (id 135329) has no threshold and no unit price computed — a build error the page renders anyway. Same pattern with brand names: the same five Muha SKUs run as “Muha Mates 5Pk – 20% Off” and “Muha Meds 5-Pack – 2/$30”.

Evidence: lume.com/specials/all · ids 135330, 135329, 135491, 135465 · observed Sep 20, 2026

C3 Data matchC1 Required fields

05

Store hours disagree across three sources on 32 of 40 store pages

Each store page shows an hours table from the Dutchie feed; the CMS record and the page's own JSON-LD say something else. Adrian: table Sun–Thu 9–8, Fri–Sat 9–10; CMS Mon–Thu 10–8:45; JSON-LD Mo-Th 10:00-20:45. Big Rapids has three different answers and a JSON-LD phone of “(248)918-43610” — eleven digits. Only 8 stores match themselves. The homepage says “38 Michigan locations”; the locations page lists 40.

Evidence: lume.com/stores/… (Adrian, Big Rapids, Cedar Springs, Menominee, New Buffalo) · /api/store-information · homepage copy · observed Sep 20, 2026

C12 Store codesC16 Wording

06

Stale promo copy still live and indexed

The Specials hub's Vendor Day Deals card lists a March/April schedule with no year, names “Mt Pleasant – Mission” and “Kalkaska” (no such stores) and spells “Broomflied”. /price-drop-10-5-24, /summer-fest, /menominee-closure (an October 2024 calendar) and /home-page (a January-2024 homepage build advertising “$20 1/8ths, $120 Oz”) all return 200, self-canonical, no noindex. Morenci's page thanks customers at “our Lansing location”; Kalamazoo's reads “:ume”.

Evidence: lume.com/specials · sitemap.xml (7,651 URLs, 1,087 duplicates) · /home-page · /stores/…morenci · observed Sep 20, 2026

C10 DatesC15 Assets

What's right

Worth keeping

Regular prices were identical for all 1,716 SKUs across the six store menus compared — no cross-store reg-price drift, which is the hardest thing to hold at 40 stores. Weekly deals carry end dates and the internal names already flag vendor funding (“(V)”), which is exactly the field a vendor-agreement check needs. The specials data is structured enough that every finding above could be a formula, not a person.

Method & scope

Public pages only, Sep 20, 2026: lume.com specials (Ann Arbor selected, spot-checked at Kalamazoo, Evart, Iron Mountain, Mt Pleasant Broomfield), the site's own page data, 40 store pages, sitemap.xml and /api/store-information. No cart was checked out, so whether checkout auto-applies the cheapest overlapping deal is not verified — the finding is that two prices are displayed. The Dutchie-hosted menus returned 403 to me, so the site's menu is the only menu compared. Whether the CMS hours text is shown to shoppers or only to search engines is unverified; the JSON-LD conflict is certain.

sheets.title: Shipping is done. Ready is the other half.
sheets.html:
Launch readiness · an outside read

A launch isn't finished when it ships; it's finished when every team is ready and every customer-facing surface says the same thing. So I read Dutchie's launches from the outside — release notes, monthly updates, help center, status page — and checked whether every surface told the same story on the same day.

Public release surfaces compared 5

Help articles for Consumer AI, 97 days in 0

Features shipped but still “Coming soon”1

Headline typos in two weeks 2

Six launch-board items

L-01No-go

One feature, three states on three official surfaces

The Aug 27 release note says chain admins “now have a single Mobile App area”; the September monthly update leads with it as shipped. The help article both link to is still titled “Coming soon: Configure and customize the Mobile App tab in Chain Admin” — and was edited on Sep 11, two weeks after GA, without the title changing.

L-02No-go

Consumer AI: 97 days after launch, no help articles

Press release and blog, June 15: Voice AI, Agentic Commerce, Register Co-Pilot and Consumer Pulse. Help-center search on Sep 20 returns zero articles for each name. The nav still badges it “🚀 new”. By contrast, Dutchie MCP — an early-access feature — has a help article updated July 29.

L-03At risk

Plus end-of-support lives only in a blog post

Aug 2025, CTO: supporting legacy Plus customers “through the end of 2026.” On Sep 10, 2026, a release note ships new Plus API support with no sunset reminder; the status page lists Plus as a live component; no public deprecation page was found. Third-party agencies now publish the “Dutchie Plus sunset” guides.

“Coming Soon: Configure and use Scan to Redeem” was created July 10. It isn't in any Aug–Sep release note I checked. Either it slipped or it shipped without an announcement; the public record can't say which — which is the problem a launch board exists to prevent.

Sep 10: “Total terpenese support” — baked into the URL slug. Sep 17: “Block checkout for unfilfilled pre-orders.” Sep 3 titles use “Dutchie POS Release Notes: …” while every other week uses “Dutchie POS: …”. Monthly-update slugs use four patterns.

dutchie.com/business · status.dutchie.com · support.dutchie.com · observed Sep 20, 2026

Name dictionary

What's working

Release notes ship every Thursday, one POS and one E-Commerce entry, without fail — that's a real operating rhythm. Monthly updates have run every month of 2026. All 58 business-site nav links return 200. And the early-access pattern for Dutchie MCP — a help article live before GA — is exactly the pattern the other launches are missing. The gap isn't process; it's that no single check confirms every surface flipped together.

Method & scope

Public sources only, Sep 20, 2026: updates.dutchie.com (page 1, Aug 13–Sep 17), the monthly-update index, the help center's public search API and Product Announcements category, status.dutchie.com (incident titles from the page's embedded data) and the Aug 2025 Plus post. developers.dutchie.com didn't resolve for me, so absence of a Plus deprecation page is “not found publicly”, not proven absent. I didn't check social channels.

What I bring, plainly. Six years of running retail platform launches and migrations end to end — two storefronts in parallel, 14,000-SKU moves with redirect maps, seasonal launches across teams. I haven't held a SaaS program-manager title; I built the gate on the next page because that's how I already work, and I'd rather you judge the gate than the title.

shot.alt: Salt Security review — sheet 02, first screen

sheets.html:
Sec. 03 — FAQPage

THE MISSING MARKUP

The FAQPage that isn't there

/api-security-101 already asks and answers questions with H2s — “What is API security?” Wrapping them in FAQPage markup is the documented way to make Q&A content extractable. Nothing changes for a human reader.

Now — /api-security-101<h2>What is API security?</h2>
<p>API security is the practice of…</p>
<h2>Why do APIs get attacked?</h2>
<p>APIs expose business logic…</p>
/* no JSON-LD — prose, not a quotable Q&A */
Fixed — same content, marked up<script type="application/ld+json">
{ "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [{ "@type": "Question",
    "name": "What is API security?",
    "acceptedAnswer": { "@type": "Answer",
      "text": "API security is the practice of…" }
  }] }
</script>

INTERACTIVE

The Webflow embed, generated

Edit a question or answer and the JSON-LD rebuilds — the same pattern as a Webflow CMS embed bound to FAQ fields, so editors never touch code.

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What is API security?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "API security is the practice of…"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Why do APIs get attacked?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "APIs expose business logic…"
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

Evidence: /api-security-101 and /blog/the-role-of-agentic-ai-in-cybersecurity (Sep 10, 2026) source; Google Search Central FAQPage docs. Answers truncated here — the embed takes the full visible text.

← Coverage

shot.alt: Salt Security review — sheet 03, first screen

sheets.html:
Sec. 04 — Signals & plan

SITEMAP ⇄ ROBOTS

2,929 submitted. 720 forbidden.

The sitemap asks Google to crawl URLs that robots.txt tells it not to — wasted crawl budget and a mixed signal.

2,209 kept & crawlable720 remove

Evidence: sitemap.xml (2,929 URLs) vs robots.txt disallowed paths /partners/, /customers/, /blog-tags/, /blog-authors/, /blog-categories/ = 720

Titles

Still “API Security”

/about-us reads “API Security Company - About Us Salt Security API Security” — legacy positioning against the agentic message. A rewrite for 12 company pages.

Typo

DienDeal / DeinDeal

/customers spells the customer “DienDeal” once vs “DeinDeal” ten times — on a page linking 32 noindex, ~38-word stubs.

AI crawlers

llms.txt

A 404 today, and robots.txt has no AI-crawler rules. llms.txt / llms-full.txt is the emerging convention and costs nothing.

FIRST 30 DAYS

The answer layer, shipped

Week 1

Schema map

  • JSON-LD embed per Webflow template (FAQPage, TechArticle, SoftwareApplication, Organization)
  • Two live FAQPage builds as proof
  • llms.txt / llms-full.txt

Weeks 2–3

Clean signals

  • Remove 720 disallowed URLs from the sitemap
  • Decide the 32 noindex customer stubs
  • Rewrite 12 “API Security” titles; fix the typo

Week 4

Measure

  • AEO dashboard: query set, engines, citation tracking
  • Keak test plan (named in your posting)
  • Search Console + Profound baseline

Method & scope — said plainly

Public data pulled Sep 19, 2026: the source of 60 sampled salt.security pages, llms.txt, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml cross-referenced against robots.txt disallowed paths. Snippets illustrate the markup I'd add, validated against Google's docs before shipping. My background is retail and B2B e-commerce, not SaaS or cybersecurity, and I haven't shipped in Webflow yet (Elementor, Divi and Shopify themes are the analog). What transfers is six years of owning sites end to end. If the schema audit is useful on its own, take it.

sheets.title: A 104,000-product catalog is only as good as its worst record.
sheets.html:
Sec. 01 — Overview · for the eCommerce Database Manager role

I sampled JB Tools' live search feed and product pages. In a 799-item slice I found double-encoded characters in product names that carry through to titles and JSON-LD, UPCs printed on the page but missing from the schema, percent-encoded schema descriptions, inconsistent attribute casing, and a torque-wrench category that is a third out of stock while sold-out items still rank in search. This is a four-page walkthrough of the defects, a working triage board, and the supplier-price SOP I'd run as your Database Manager.

104,348 products in the live Searchspring index (the About page still says “beyond 60,000”)

8/799 sampled names with encoding artifacts — in H1, title and JSON-LD

122/358 torque wrenches out of stock (34%); a sold-out item ranks #3 in search

0 gtin in Product schema, though UPCs are shown on the page

The job

What this role owns

“Manage and maintain our catalog of tens of thousands of products across hundreds of suppliers… pricing, UPCs, SKUs, weights, dimensions, descriptions, images, specifications… supplier spreadsheets and large datasets… Excel/Google Sheets and AI tools.”

That is the job I've done: 14,000+ SKUs migrated and maintained by CSV, attribute mapping and QA.

Why it matters

Defects reach the shopper & the feed

Encoding artifacts show up in SERP titles. A missing gtin blocks clean Google Merchant Center matching. A sold-out item at #3 in search is a dead end at the top of results — the kind of thing behind the BBB complaint mix (Product 15 of 50).

The approach

Census → fix → prevent

A full-catalog defect census, a fix-priority board weighted by price and stock, a schema patch that reaches every product at once, a sold-out policy, and a supplier price-change intake so a price file becomes a validated import — not a manual afternoon.

Scope jbtools.com public catalog Method Searchspring API sample (799 items) + PDP source + Lighthouse Platform BigCommerce Stencil · Searchspring · Yotpo · Klaviyo Independent — not affiliated with JB Tools

sheets.html:
Sec. 02 — The defect census

FIVE CLASSES

What the catalog is telling Google

Five defect classes, each found in the live data, each a line item in the Database Manager job description. Counts are from a 799-product sample of the public Searchspring feed unless noted; percentages describe the sample, not the full 104,348-product catalog — the full run is deliverable #1.

Encoding

Mojibake in names

“Nano Flex Ratcheting Attachment Set 14â€“19mm (NORA150XL)” — a double-encoded en-dash, live in the H1 and the JSON-LD name. 8 of 799 sampled names carry artifacts (1/4\x94, Airlift\x99).

Evidence: /vim-tools-nano-flex-ratcheting-attachment-set-14-19mm-nora150xl/ ; Searchspring search.json

Schema

UPC shown, no gtin

The OTC 7378 page displays “UPC: 731413001376” but the Product JSON-LD has no gtin; its description is percent-encoded and priceValidUntil is hard-coded.

Evidence: /otc-7378-torque-wrench-50-250/ source

Consistency

Attribute casing

The custom availability attribute is cased three ways in the sample — “US” 247, “us” 103, blank 449 — so any rule that keys on it silently misses a third of rows.

Evidence: Searchspring sample of 799 items

Naming

Part-number convention

133 of 799 names omit the “(part #)” convention the rest of the catalog follows, which weakens exact-match search and Merchant Center matching.

Evidence: Searchspring sample

Taxonomy

Miscategorized items

A “Wiha 14-Piece SoftFinish Screwdriver Set” sits under Hand Tools › Wrenches › Torque Wrenches › Torque Wrench Accessories. Facets are only In Stock / Brand / Price — no drive size, torque range or type.

Evidence: /wiha-14-piece-softfinish-screwdriver-set-30284/ ; /torque-wrenches/ facets

Availability

Sold-out still ranking

Torque Wrenches: 358 items, 122 “Out of Stock” (34%). The sold-out OTC 7378 ranks #3 in native search for “torque wrench” — a dead end at the top of results.

Evidence: /torque-wrenches/ facet counts ; native search

The schema patch

One template change fixes every product that has this defect — and it's the change that decides whether 104k listings match cleanly in Google Merchant Center. Google requires gtin for products that have one; you already display the UPC.

Now — /otc-7378-torque-wrench-50-250/{
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "OTC 7378 Torque Wrench 50-250",
  "description": "The%20OTC%20Accutorq…",
  "sku": "OTC7378",
  /* no gtin — UPC 731413001376 in page text only */
  "offers": {
    "priceValidUntil": "2027-09-19",
    "availability": "…OutOfStock"
  }
}
Patched template{
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "OTC 7378 Torque Wrench 50-250",
  "description": "The OTC Accutorq…",
  "sku": "OTC7378",
  "gtin12": "731413001376",
  "mpn": "7378",
  "offers": {
    "priceValidUntil": "{{dynamic +1yr}}",
    "availability": "…OutOfStock"
  }
}

Evidence: OTC 7378 PDP source; Google Merchant Center product-data spec (gtin required where it exists).

sheets.html:
Sec. 04 — Plan & method

SOLD-OUT

Handling out-of-stock

A third of a flagship category is out of stock and still ranking. Discontinued products should leave the catalog; temporarily-out products should stay discoverable but stop occupying the top of search.

Rank

Demote, don't hide

Out-of-stock items drop below in-stock in Searchspring relevance so no sold-out product ranks #3 for a head term. They stay indexable for the long tail.

Recover

“Notify me” by default

Every out-of-stock PDP defaults to the In-Stock-Notify app already installed, turning a dead end into a captured email + a Klaviyo back-in-stock flow.

Retire

Discontinued = deactivate + 301

Supplier-discontinued SKUs are deactivated and 301'd to the closest live equivalent or the parent category, so the gap analysis against supplier files actually closes.

SOP

Supplier price-change intake

The job is “process supplier price changes” and “gap analysis between supplier catalogs and products listed on our stores.” Here's the intake I'd stand up — Excel + AI-assisted, as the posting asks.

Step 1 · Normalize

Ingest

  • Supplier file → fixed column map (UPC, cost, MSRP, MAP, status)
  • AI-assisted cleanup of units, encoding and stray characters before anything touches the store
  • Rows keyed on UPC/MPN, not name

Step 2 · Reconcile

Gap analysis

  • Diff supplier list against the live Searchspring index
  • Flag: new items, discontinued, price deltas beyond a threshold, MAP violations
  • Nothing auto-publishes — the diff is reviewed first

Step 3 · Publish

Validated import

  • BigCommerce CSV import with a pre-flight validation pass (my Commerce Change Atlas pattern)
  • Post-import spot-check on price, availability and schema
  • Every change logged for rollback

I built this before: Commerce Change Atlas diffs supplier files against live listings before they load — lab.mousabatarseh.com. At Universal Wholesale I ran the same motion on 14,000+ SKUs by CSV.

90 DAYS

First 90 days

Days 1–30

Census

  • Full-catalog defect run (all 104k, not a sample)
  • Ship the schema patch (gtin, decoded description, mpn, rolling date)
  • Fix the visible mojibake in the highest-traffic categories first

Days 31–60

Systematize

  • Attribute-casing normalization + part-number convention pass
  • Sold-out demotion + “notify me” default live
  • Supplier price-change SOP running weekly

Days 61–90

Prevent

  • Facets that match the category (drive size, torque range, type)
  • Discontinued-item retirement + 301 loop closing the supplier gap
  • A weekly data-health report so defects are caught, not discovered

Method & scope

Every number here comes from public data pulled on Sep 19, 2026: the Searchspring search API that powers jbtools.com search and category grids (a 799-product sample, siteId 77jpy6), individual product-page source (JSON-LD, H1, displayed UPC), the /torque-wrenches/ facet counts, and a Lighthouse mobile audit. Sampled percentages describe the sample, not the full 104,348-product catalog — the first deliverable is the full run. I'm not affiliated with JB Tools; this is an independent review to show how I'd approach the eCommerce Database Manager role, and I'd validate every finding against the actual product feed and admin, which expose fields (weights, dimensions, cost) the public catalog doesn't.

Sec. 02 — Findings

STORE PAGES

The pages that don't exist

A 275-store retailer's biggest local-SEO asset is a page per store. Today there is none — and the locator hides the data from crawlers entirely.

sheets.html:
The eComm Manager job asks for a weekly note that says what happened, why, where we are against target, and what we'll do. I don't have your numbers yet, so I read everything else. This is dehanche.com as it rendered on September 16, 2026, every one of its 164 live products run through a catalog check, and the tools I'd run the role with.

Read the twelve flags Open the catalog scanner See the worked examples

Scan slip 16 · IX · 2026

Live products checked
164
Size variants · in stock
516 / 631
Product images with their own alt text
0 / 722
Distinct product tags
375
Products tagged both 24K and 18K gold

“All Belts” pages in the sitemap
