Slot 10 of All Belts
Sold out

Public storefront only: product JSON, collection pages, sitemap, rendered pages on mobile and desktop. No login, no internal data.

The report · four parts, as the posting asks

The week, in brief.

Same format I'd send every Monday. This week's version is built from what a customer, a search engine and a scraper can see.

i.

What happened

The Fall 2026 drop is live and the product pages read beautifully. Underneath, the storefront has drifted: a sold-out belt in a top slot, a “Pre-Order” page selling sale stock, three copies of All Belts, and tags that contradict the product.

ii.

Why it matters

Each of these costs clicks, trust or rankings, and none needs a developer to fix. Most trace back to product data: tags, types and alt text feed the filters, feeds, search and email segments.

iii.

Against target

Unknown from the outside. Below is the pacing board I'd set up on day one, running on sample numbers until it's connected to Shopify.

iv.

What we'll do

This week: fix slot order, retire the Pre-Order page, redirect the duplicate collections, start the tag-to-metafield cleanup. Next: the size-row and second-belt tests, then two new email flows with the Klaviyo team.

Product copy

PDP titles and descriptions are specific and on-brand: “Hollyhock Black Silver Belt | Déhanche”, cast in Italy, ten holes, lined in suede.

Stock health

516 of 631 size variants are in stock and only 4 of 164 products are fully sold out. There's plenty of product to merchandise.

Size-level states

The theme already knows “Available”, “Low Availability” and “Pre-Order” per size, and has Klaviyo waitlist hooks wired in.

The right stack

Algolia search, Rebuy recommendations, Global-e, Klaviyo, Clarity, Triple Whale. Nothing new to buy, just tuning.

Clear offers

Free US ground shipping over $250 and 15% off two full-price belts are both good AOV levers.

Editorial pull

The imagery and storytelling carry the brand. The fixes below should protect that, not dilute it.

What happened · twelve flags

Found before anyone flagged them.

Each flag shows what I saw, why it costs sales or trust, and the fix. Everything was captured from the public storefront on September 16, 2026. Screenshots are cropped, not edited.

01 HighMerchandising · /collections/belts

A sold-out belt sits in slot 10 of All Belts. The $250 best sellers sit at 33 and 34.

/collections/belts · rendered at 1440px · Sept 16Slot 10 → SOLD OUT Hollyhock Crystal Black Silver · $495 · 0 of 5 sizes tagged: Best seller · New Arrivals · Fall26 Slot 27 → Mija Black Silver · $290 · Best Seller badge Slot 33 → Constance Black Silver · $250 · Best Seller badge Slot 34 → Constance Black Gold · $250 · Best Seller badge (ninth row, ~6,300px down)

The first three rows take most of the clicks. A sold-out tile there is a dead end, and Constance at $250 is the easiest first purchase in the line.

Fix

Sold-out products drop to the end automatically, and their tile offers the waitlist instead. In-stock best sellers at each price tier ($250 / $290 / $325) are pinned into the first twelve slots. I'd review the order weekly against sell-through.

Owner eComm Effort 1 hour Measure collection CTR, PDP views per session

02 HighMerchandising · /collections/pre-order

The “Pre-Order” page is selling final-sale stock.

/collections/pre-order · public · listed in sitemap_collections8 products, all purchasable now Hollyhock Ochre Suede Gold $325 → $180 final sale Versailles Ochre Suede Gold $425 → $350 final sale Cupid Black Gold $350 → $249 final sale Versailles Black Gold · Vendome Black Gold tagged Preorder · Prefall25 · published Feb 2026 PDP size states for Versailles Black Gold: Available / Low Availability (none Pre-Order)

A shopper who lands here from search, an old email or an ad reads “pre-order” and expects to wait. Instead they get in-stock belts, some of them final sale and non-returnable. The posting names this exact problem: an in-stock product showing as pre-order.

Fix

Let inventory drive pre-order status. The theme already reads a per-size Pre-Order state from Fabrikator. Rebuild the collection as “tag Preorder AND not in stock”, remove the tag from styles that have shipped, and redirect the page to New Arrivals whenever it's empty.

Owner eComm + Ops Effort half a day Measure zero in-stock items in Pre-Order

03 MediumMerchandising · /collections/new-arrivals

“New Arrivals” goes back almost a year.

/collections/new-arrivals · 57 products · publish dates from products.jsonpublished > 90 days ago 17 published > 180 days ago 7 oldest 323 days still tagged “New Arrivals”: Bodice Belt Black Short (created May 2025), Vendome Black Gold, Vendome Ivory Gold, Élysées Gold Chain Belt (Jan 2026) 2 of the 57 are fully sold out (Hollyhock Crystal Black Silver, Signet Stone Hinge Earring Onyx & Silver)

Regulars stop checking “New” when it doesn't change, and the Fall 2026 pieces get buried among older ones.

Fix

Make the collection automatic: published in the last 60 days, in stock. Pin the hero launch pieces by hand and drop the manual tag.

Owner eComm Effort 1 hour Measure New Arrivals CTR, repeat-visitor sessions

04 HighCatalog data · tags

The tags contradict the products.

tags across all 164 live productsdistinct tags: 375 gold alone: Gold · Gold Finish · Gold Hardware · Gold Metal · Gold-Plated · Gold-Tone · 24K Gold · 18K Gold tagged both 24K Gold and 18K Gold: 34 products Hollyhock Crystal Black Silver: tagged Gold, Silver, 24K Gold and 18K Gold internal tags visible to anyone: Check_COGS · HIDE_IN_FABRIKATOR · black_crow_do_not_cross_sell · nyla_filter_Price_300399 · “260”

Filters, the Google feed, search and email segments all read these tags. A karat filter that returns silver belts loses trust, and conflicting karat data is a product-claims risk on a luxury site.

Fix

Move product facts into metafields with one allowed value each: metal (Silver / 24K gold-plated / Mixed), leather, width, collection family. Tags stay for merchandising only. Internal tags get an underscore prefix and a written owner, so the next person knows what's safe to delete. The scanner below lists every affected product.

Owner eComm + Product Effort 2–3 days, bulk CSV Measure filter zero-result rate, feed disapprovals

05 MediumCatalog data · product records

Gaps in product records break the tools downstream.

products.json · 164 products · 631 variantsno product type 18 products: all 8 men's belts, Brancusi cuffs, Élysées bracelet, Rosen, Mila, Santo Enamel… vendor spelled 2 ways “DÉHANCHE” ×95 · “Déhanche” ×69 shippable, weight 0 g 260 variants no SKU 13 variants

Product type drives Google Shopping categories and category reporting. Zero weights can misprice shipping and Global-e duty quotes. Missing SKUs break inventory syncs and wholesale reconciliation.

Fix

One bulk CSV pass (Matrixify or the Shopify bulk editor), plus a required-fields check before any product goes live. That check is item one on the launch checklist below.

Owner eComm Effort half a day Measure 0 blank types, 0 zero-weight variants

06 HighCatalog data · SEO · accessibility

Every image of a product says the same thing.

products.json · Hollyhock Black Silver product page HTMLcatalog alt text filled in: 0 of 722 images the theme falls back to the product title, so on the Hollyhock Black Silver page all 18 images read: alt="Hollyhock Black Silver" (front, side, buckle detail and on-model shots are indistinguishable)

Screen-reader shoppers hear the same name eighteen times. Google Images, a real discovery channel for visual luxury goods, gets one repeated phrase. Feeds read the empty field, and missing or identical alt text often appears in ADA demand letters.

Fix

Fill alt text from a template in one bulk pass: “Hollyhock belt in black calfskin with silver five-ring hardware, front view”, then “…, worn at the waist”, and so on. Add it to the launch checklist so new products ship with it.

Owner eComm + Creative Effort 1 day with a script Measure Google Images clicks in Search Console

07 MediumSEO · collections

Three “All Belts” pages compete with each other.

title tags · canonical · sitemap_collections_1.xml/collections/belts “Shop All Belts – Made in Italy | Déhanche” canonical → itself /collections/all-belts-copy “Shop All Belts – Made in Italy | Déhanche” canonical → itself /collections/belts-all “Shop All Belts | Déhanche” canonical → itself identical meta descriptions on the first two · all three listed in the sitemap

Google splits ranking signals across near-duplicates and can pick the copy to rank.

Fix

301 /all-belts-copy to /belts. Keep /belts-all (the full-price view) out of the index, or give it a distinct purpose and title. One All Belts page holds the rankings.

Owner eComm Effort 30 minutes Measure impressions consolidate on /belts

08 MediumSEO · housekeeping

Internal and expired collections are public and in the sitemap.

61 collections in sitemap_collections · page titles as served/sizing-source-collection title “sizing source collection” · 53 products shown /wholesale-only title “Wholesale Only” · 0 products /catalog title “Collection” /international-womens-month a March campaign, still live in September /pre-fall-24 · /pre-spring-25 · /fall-collection (titled “Fall 2025”) /resort-2027 no products visible yet

Empty and internal pages sit in the index, shoppers can reach them, and old seasons can outrank the current one.

Fix

Unpublish the utility collections from the Online Store, or noindex them through the template. Redirect past seasons to the current season, hold Resort 2027 until launch day, and audit collections once a quarter.

Owner eComm Effort 2 hours Measure indexed pages in Search Console

09 LowSEO · homepage

The homepage title is only the brand name.

view-source: dehanche.com<title>Déhanche</title> <h1>Déhanche | </h1> (a stray pipe after the name) compare: product pages → “Hollyhock Black Silver Belt | Déhanche”

Fix

Title: “Déhanche | Sculptural Italian Leather Belts & Jewelry”, and a clean H1. It takes two minutes and lets the homepage rank for more than the brand name.

10 MediumPDP · conversion

Size is the first question about a belt, and the product page hides it.

/products/hollyhock-black-silver · iPhone-sized viewportsizes XS–XXL and “Low Availability” appear only after tapping Add to Cart the “BESTSELLER” badge renders on top of the header icons Afterpay and Klarna scripts load, but no installment line shows under $325

Shoppers who can't see their size or its stock before committing hesitate. “Only one left in XL” works as urgency only if people see it.

Fix

Show the size row with stock state above Add to Cart (A/B test, T1 below). Fix the badge's z-index. Test an installment line on items over $250.

Owner eComm + Dev Effort 2–3 days Measure add-to-cart rate, size exchanges

11 MediumAOV · bag and homepage

The best offer on the site only shows in the top banner.

announcement bar · bag drawer · homepagebar rotates: “15% OFF TWO OR MORE FULL PRICED BELTS” bag says: “Complimentary shipping on orders over $250.00.” with no progress bar and no second-belt prompt homepage: four editorial blocks, no shoppable product row

The offer is there to raise order value, but no one sees it when they add a first belt, which is when it would matter.

Fix

Add a bag nudge: “Add a second belt, save 15%”, with Rebuy suggestions limited to in-stock sizes and the other hardware finish of the same style. Test a shoppable Hollyhock row under the hero against the editorial layout (T2 and T5).

Owner eComm Effort 1–2 days Measure AOV, units per order

12 MediumPerformance · tags

Heavy pages: three copies of one 1080p video, a doubled GA4 tag, 30+ third parties.

Lighthouse 12, mobile, lab run from a cloud server (directional) · page source · resource timingHollyhock Black Silver page: 3 autoplaying <video> tags for the same 1080p 7.2 Mbps file · 26.7 MB total transfer Performance score: homepage 31 · product page 26 (LCP 6.2 s / 21.9 s) third-party main-thread blocking ≈ 5.9 s: Google Tag Manager 2.9 s · Facebook 0.9 s · Klaviyo 0.5 s · Rebuy 0.5 s · Yandex Metrica 0.2 s two GTM containers (GTM-KSX9D6X, GTM-P8P6WVRR) · GA4 G-Q891RMV74D loaded twice New Arrivals: 546 requests · 5,514 DOM elements

Luxury traffic arrives mostly on phones, from Instagram and email, and a slow first product page loses sales. A doubled GA4 tag can also double-count, which undermines the weekly numbers.

Fix

Load the video once, at 720p on mobile with a poster image. Consolidate to one GTM container, remove unused pixels (why is Yandex Metrica there?), and delay below-the-fold apps. Confirm the gains with field data (Search Console Core Web Vitals, CrUX) before and after.

Owner eComm + Dev Effort 1 week Measure mobile LCP, INP, conversion rate

Every product, checked every morning.

Email · six flow concepts for the Klaviyo team

Use sales data to time every send.

The posting asks the eComm Manager to use real-time sales, product and customer data to shape email. These are six places where that data changes what gets sent and when. All are concepts to build with the email team, using products and prices from the live site.

01 · Your size is back

Recovered revenue

  1. Trigger: a back-in-stock request for one size.e.g. Constance Black Silver, size S, sold out today
  2. Email when that size restocks. Subject: “Your size is back: Constance, S”.instant
  3. Reminder only if the shopper hasn't bought and two or fewer are left: “Two left in S”.+24 hours
  4. Exit when they order that size.

requested back-in-stock · variant option = S AND not ordered variant since request

02 · The second belt

AOV · repeat rate

  1. Trigger: an order with exactly one full-price belt.
  2. Wait until the belt has been worn once.delivered + 3 days
  3. Email: “Two belts, fifteen percent”. It leads with the other finish of the same style, e.g. Constance Black Silver → Constance Black Gold, $250.
  4. Skip anyone with a return or exchange open; send at most once every 90 days.

placed order · belts_full_price = 1 AND NOT return_started · last 90 days

03 · Match the hardware

Jewelry attach

  1. Trigger: a belt delivered three weeks ago.
  2. Branch on the metal metafield: silver, gold or mixed.
  3. Email: “The same five rings, for your ears”. A Hollyhock Black Silver buyer sees Hollyhock Silver Earrings Medium, $320.
  4. Stop once they've bought jewelry in that finish.

delivered belt · 21 days ago metal = metafield(custom.metal) ← needs flag 04 cleanup

04 · Fit, before doubt

Conversion

  1. Trigger: opened “Find my fit” but didn't add to cart.+2 hours, known subscribers
  2. Email: how sizing works. Measure where you'll wear it (waist or hips); ten holes follow the figure; exchanges are easy.
  3. Add a stock note if the viewed style has Low Availability in any size.
  4. Exit on add to cart.

custom event “Viewed Fit Guide” (from the sizing sheet) AND NOT Added to Cart within 2h

05 · First access

Launch-day revenue

  1. Trigger: a launch date, e.g. Resort 2027 (the collection already exists).
  2. VIP link to customers with 2+ orders or one of $500+, plus the collection's waitlist.launch − 24 h
  3. General send: the lookbook, then the shop.launch day
  4. Sizes going fast: only styles with two or fewer left in any size.+48 h

VIP = orders ≥ 2 OR max_order ≥ $500 “going fast” = any size inventory ≤ 2

06 · The pace-keeper

Close the gap

  1. Trigger: the pacing board shows month-to-date more than 8% behind by the 15th.
  2. Send a pre-built campaign to subscribers who engaged but haven't bought in 90 days.
  3. Feature best sellers with full size runs only, never final sale, with no discount on core styles.
  4. Cap at once a month; the report records what it recovered.

IF mtd_revenue < 0.92 × pace(day 15) THEN schedule campaign “Hollyhock, all sizes”

Flow 01, written out

A short, specific email with one action.

Subject: Your size is back: Constance, S
Preview: Constance Black Silver · S · back in stock today.

It names the exact size, shows one product, and has one button that opens the page with size S already selected. It doesn't discount the belt.

Its value is measured as revenue per back-in-stock request, and it's only a good report number if flag 01's waitlist tiles are feeding it.

briefing a developer

How I'd hand two of the flags to a developer: context with evidence, a clear scope, acceptance criteria that can be tested, and how we'll know it worked. Ready to paste into Jira, Linear or an email.

DEH-101 · Merchandising · from flag 01

Sold-out products drop to the end of collection grids, and their tiles offer the waitlist

Priority High Effort 1–2 days Spec & QA eComm Build Developer

Context

Collection order is set by hand, so sold-out products stay where they were placed. On September 16, slot 10 of All Belts was a belt sold out in all five sizes, while the $250 best sellers sat at slots 33 and 34.

/collections/belts · desktop 1440px · Sept 16Slot 10 → SOLD OUT Hollyhock Crystal Black Silver · $495 · 0 of 5 sizes
Slot 33 → Constance Black Silver · $250 · Best Seller badge
Slot 34 → Constance Black Gold · $250 · Best Seller badge
Build
  1. Products with no available size move after every in-stock product, in every collection grid. The hand-set order of in-stock products doesn't change.
  2. A sold-out tile shows “Join the waitlist” and opens the back-in-stock form for that product. No price-only dead end.
  3. When any size comes back, the product returns to its hand-set position.
Approach

Sort where the grid is built. If Algolia renders collection pages, rank on an in-stock attribute there. If Shopify does, use a sold-out-last app or a small job that calls the Admin API's collectionReorderProducts when inventory changes. Don't sort in Liquid per page, because that breaks across pages.

Done when
  • Given a product with zero available sizes, when any collection page loads, then it appears after all products with at least one size available.
  • Given an in-stock product in slot 5, when another product sells out, then its order relative to the other in-stock products is unchanged.
  • Given a sold-out product restocks one size, when the next inventory sync runs, then it's back in its hand-set slot within 15 minutes.
  • Given a sold-out tile, then it shows “Join the waitlist” and no add-to-cart, on mobile and desktop, with filters applied.
QA
  • On a duplicate theme, set a test product's stock to 0 and check All Belts, Best Sellers and New Arrivals.
  • Restock one size and confirm it moves back.
  • Run Lighthouse on All Belts before and after to confirm the page isn't slower.
Measure & rollback
  • Collection click-through, add-to-cart rate from collections, waitlist sign-ups, compared over two weeks before and after.
  • Rollback: switch the app off or republish the previous theme.
  • Out of scope: pinning best sellers by price tier. That's a merchandising task, done by hand.

DEH-102 · Analytics · from flag 12

One GA4 tag, one Tag Manager container

Priority High Effort half a day Spec & QA eComm Build Developer + Marketing

Context

Two Tag Manager containers load on every page, and the GA4 property loads twice. Page views and events can be counted twice, which makes every weekly number less reliable. It also adds main-thread time on phones.

page source · Lighthouse 12 mobile (lab) · Sept 16GTM-KSX9D6X · GTM-P8P6WVRR → two containers
G-Q891RMV74D → loaded twice
Google Tag Manager main-thread time ≈ 2.9 s · Yandex Metrica present
Build
  1. Audit both containers with marketing. List every tag, its owner and whether it's still used.
  2. Move the tags that are still needed into one container and remove the other snippet from the theme.
  3. Confirm the purchase event fires once through Shopify's customer events.
  4. Remove pixels no one owns, such as Yandex Metrica, after marketing confirms.
Done when
  • Given the homepage, a collection, a product page and checkout, when Tag Assistant runs, then it shows one GA4 configuration for G-Q891RMV74D.
  • Given a test order, when it completes, then GA4 DebugView shows exactly one purchase event.
  • Given any page load, then DebugView shows one page_view.
Measure & note

GA4 sessions and page views will drop when duplicates stop. I'd mark the change date in the weekly note so no one reads it as a real decline, and compare conversion with Shopify's own numbers for two weeks.

sheets.html:
The Senior E-Commerce Specialist keeps Hay House's Shopify storefronts accurate, fast and easy to shop. Before applying, I read shop.hayhouse.com the way I would in my first week: all 874 products, the filters, the pages, the structured data, the speed, and how it lines up with hayhouse.com. Everything here comes from public pages on September 16, 2026.

Read the twelve findings Run the catalog check See the worked examples

Catalog card 16 SEP 2026

5

861 / 878

5,623

Descriptive alt text (220-image sample)
0
Worthy: hayhouse.com vs here
$9.50 / $18.99

Public sources only: products.json, product .js, rendered pages, sitemaps, robots.txt and /.well-known/ucp. No logins, no internal data.

The report · four parts

The storefront, in brief.

The same shape I'd use for a weekly note to the Director of E-Commerce: what's working, what needs attention, why it matters, and what I'd do first.

i.

What's working

The migration landed: 816 titles were created in April and new releases have been added every month since, with ISBN SKUs, book-detail metafields, an Authors filter and Shop Pay Installments. Shopify's agent endpoints are already on.

ii.

What needs attention

Some data came over from Magento with gaps: two prices for the same book across Hay House sites, duplicate listings, filters that split formats and authors, zero weights, templated alt text and 5,623 tags.

iii.

Why it matters

Filters, Google Shopping, social catalogs, shipping rates and AI shopping agents all read the same product data. Clean it once and every channel improves at the same time.

iv.

What I'd do first

Week one: agree the price of record, merge duplicates, fix the Format and Authors filters, add weights. Then H1s and book structured data with the developers, tags into metafields, and alt text in batches.

ISBNs as SKUs

All 878 variants use an ISBN-13 as the SKU, and every one passes the check-digit test. That makes matching, feeds and redirects much easier.

Book details

Product pages already show pages, language, publication date, ISBN and publisher from metafields, and the Authors filter is live.

Agent-ready plumbing

Shopify publishes /agents.md, an agentic discovery sitemap and a UCP profile (2026-08-25) for the store, so AI shopping agents can search the catalog and start checkouts that the buyer approves.

What I found · twelve findings

Found before anyone had to ask.

Each finding shows what I saw, why it costs sales or trust, and the fix. The evidence comes from the public storefront on September 16, 2026. The screenshots are cropped, not edited.

01 HighPricing · two storefronts

The same book has two prices on two Hay House sites.

hayhouse.com (Magento) vs shop.hayhouse.com (Shopify) · Sept 16Worthy · PB · 9781401950156          $9.50 vs $18.99
Divine Masters, Ancient Wisdom · HC      $9.50 vs $18.99
F**K It Therapy · PB · list $15.99      $8.00, out of stock vs $19.99
You Can Heal Your Life · PB            $14.39 vs $17.99
14 of 14 ISBNs I compared cost 20–60% less on hayhouse.com
Google indexes product pages on both domains

A reader who arrives on the Shopify page from Google, Instagram or an AI assistant can pay nearly twice what hayhouse.com charges for the same ISBN. Shoppers and price-comparing agents will find both pages.

Fix

Agree which storefront is the price of record and sync the other from it, through a scheduled price sync or one product feed. If the gap is deliberate (a web-only discount, for example), show it the same way on both sites. Until then, give the pair one canonical URL so they stop competing in search.

Owner Director of E-Commerce + eComm Effort a decision, then 1 day Measure price mismatches in the weekly check (target 0)

02 HighCatalog data · duplicates

Duplicate listings split sales, reviews and rankings.

products.json · 874 products · Sept 16embrace-your-power and embrace-your-power-1
  same ISBN 9781401955892, same price $14.99
you-can-heal-your-life   PB 1984 edition · $17.99
you-can-heal-your-life-1 40th Anniversary Edition · $19.99
  both titled "You Can Heal Your Life"
5 titles appear twice · Worthy HC and PB are two products,
while Super Attractor sells the PB and the card deck
as two variants of one product

Two identical titles look like a mistake in collections, search, Google and agent answers. Inventory and reviews split across the pair, and the "-1" handles give away the import.

Fix

Merge the two Embrace Your Power listings and 301 the spare handle. Rename the anniversary edition ("You Can Heal Your Life: 40th Anniversary Edition") and link editions with an "Also available" block. Pick one rule for formats: one product per ISBN, with editions linked through a metafield, and never a card deck as a variant of a book.

Owner eComm Effort half a day Measure duplicate ISBNs and titles (target 0)

03 HighFilters · format

The Format filter lists ISBNs as formats.

/collections/mind-body-spirit · Format filter · Sept 16Card Deck (155)

A reader who filters for card decks misses those four. Paperbacks sit under two labels that mean the same thing to a customer; "Trade Paperback Original" is a publishing term.

Fix

Rename the four option values to "Card Deck" and keep the ISBN in the SKU. Show one customer-facing "Paperback" value, and keep the publishing detail in a format metafield for reports and feeds.

Owner eComm Effort 1 hour Measure filter values per format (target 1)

HH-201 · Story

One author, one filter value: move authors to Author entries

Type Data model and theme Priority High Size M, about one sprint Owner Development, with eComm for data cleanup Fixes Finding 04

Problem

Authors are stored as free text, so the same person shows up under several spellings and co-authors sit inside one value. Shoppers who pick one spelling miss the rest of the author's books.

filter.p.m.custom.authors · Sept 16David R. Hawkins, M.D. Ph.D.     5
David R. Hawkins, M.D., Ph.D.   15
Alberto Villoldo: 5 values
Steven D. Farmer: 2 values
Scope
  1. Create an Author metaobject: name, sort name, credentials, bio, photo, website. Turn on web pages for it.
  2. Add a product metafield custom.author_refs, a list of Author references. Keep custom.authors for the byline until launch.
  3. Write a one-time Admin API script: split the text on " and ", " with " and ", with "; move ", Ph.D." and ", M.D." into credentials; match each name to one Author; write the references. Unmatched rows go to an exceptions CSV.
  4. Point the Authors filter in Search & Discovery at the new metafield.
  5. Build the author page template (name as H1, photo, bio, product grid) and link the byline on product pages to it.

Out of scope: how credentials appear in the byline. That stays as it is.

Acceptance criteria
  • Given the Mind, Body, Spirit collection, when I open the Authors filter, then David R. Hawkins appears once, with 20 products.
  • Given a deck by Alberto Villoldo and Colette Baron-Reid, when I filter by either author, then the deck is in both results.
  • Given any author page, then it has exactly one H1 (the author's name), a product grid and a self-referencing canonical URL.
  • Given the exceptions CSV, then every row is resolved by eComm before launch.
QA plan
  • Run the script on a duplicate theme first and compare product counts per author before and after. No product may lose an author.
  • Spot-check 20 co-authored products and the filter on a phone.
  • Launch in a low-traffic window, then watch filter use and searches with no results for 48 hours.
  • Rollback: the old text metafield stays until the new filter has run for two weeks.

HH-202 · Task

One H1 per page, and book details in the structured data

Type Theme (Bookraze)Priority High Size S, two to three days with QA Owner Development Fixes Findings 09 and 10

Problem

Product and collection pages have no H1; the product title is an <h2 class="h2">. The home page H1 is empty. The Product markup has the SKU and brand "Hay House LLC" but no GTIN, ISBN, author, format or page count, although Book Details shows most of them on the page.

Scope
  1. Product page: render the title as <h1>. Keep the quick-add heading as h2.
  2. Collection page: add the collection title as H1. Home page: fill the H1 without changing the design.
  3. Replace the product JSON-LD with the snippet below: Product plus Book for books and journals, Product only for decks and calendars.
  4. Question for Marketing: should the brand read "Hay House" instead of "Hay House LLC" in Google Shopping?
Acceptance criteria
  • Given any product or collection page, then the HTML has exactly one h1 and it matches the title.
  • Given /products/you-can-heal-your-life-1, when I run Google's Rich Results Test, then Product is valid with no errors and gtin13 is 9781401976910.
  • Given a card deck, then the markup is Product only, with gtin13 and no Book fields.
  • Given the Schema.org validator, then the Book node shows isbn, author, bookFormat, numberOfPages and datePublished.
QA plan
  • Ten pages on a duplicate theme: five books, three decks, two journals. Rich Results Test and the Schema.org validator on each.
  • Check the quick-add modal and the cart drawer still show their headings.
  • Compare the Lighthouse SEO score before and after, then watch Search Console's product snippets report for two weeks.

{%- assign v = product.selected_or_first_available_variant -%}
{%- assign isbn = v.barcode | remove: '-' | default: v.sku -%}
{%- assign fmt = v.option1 -%}
{%- assign is_book = true -%}
{%- if fmt contains 'Card' or fmt contains 'Calendar' -%}
  {%- assign is_book = false -%}
{%- endif -%}
<script type="application/ld+json">
{

  "description": {{ product.description | strip_html | truncate: 480 | json }},
  "sku": {{ v.sku | json }},

  {%- endfor -%}],

Real URLs · status and ISBN checked Sept 16

Mapping rules

  1. Match on the ISBN from the Magento export, never on the URL text. 1,271 legacy slugs end in -1, -2 and so on, and "ask-and-it-is-given-2" is the deck, not the book.
  2. Every category path for a product (/shop/…, /shop-by-topic/…, /shop/featured/…) goes to the same Shopify page.
  3. Ebooks, audio and courses stay where they're sold today.
  4. One hop only: no chains from old path to root URL to Shopify.
  5. No match means a decision, not a redirect to the home page.

Where the redirects live

While hayhouse.com stays on Magento, the 301s belong on hayhouse.com (Magento URL rewrites or server rules). If store paths ever move to the Shopify domain, they become Shopify URL redirects, imported by CSV. Shopify only applies a redirect when the old path doesn't exist on the store.

Redirect from,Redirect to

QA before and after launch

  1. Before: crawl every legacy URL and save the status, canonical and ISBN. That crawl is how the Worthy canonical above turned up.
  2. After: crawl again. Each URL must return one 301 to a 200 page with the same ISBN.
  3. Keep the old sitemap submitted in Search Console for a few weeks so Google re-crawls it, and watch the 404 report.
  4. In GA4, list landing pages that end in 404 every week for the first month and fix them.
  5. Tell Customer Service which URLs changed, in case readers call about old links.

Same method I'd use to bring another storefront onto Shopify: inventory, ISBN match, decisions log, redirect import, re-crawl.

06 · AI workflow

From the posting

Use approved AI and automation tools, including ChatGPT Enterprise, to improve workflows, merchandising, efficiency, discoverability, and customer experience while maintaining appropriate human oversight.

Image alt text is a good first job for ChatGPT Enterprise. In a sample of 220 product images, 211 had templated alt text ("Title - image 3"), 9 repeated the title, and none described the image. Here's the workflow I'd run, with the human checks built in.

  1. 1 · ExportProducts, formats and image URLs from the Admin API, 50 products per batch.
  2. 2 · PromptChatGPT Enterprise gets the image plus title, author, format and image position. Nothing else.
  3. 3 · ValidateA script checks length, the exact title and author, banned phrases and the JSON shape.
  4. 4 · ReviewA person reads every result in the first 50, then 1 in 10. Flagged items always get a review.
  5. 5 · ImportApproved text goes back through the Admin API or the bulk editor.
  6. 6 · LogPrompt version, reviewer, date, before and after. Any change can be rolled back.

Prompt

You write alt text for product images on shop.hayhouse.com.
Input: one image, plus TITLE, AUTHOR, FORMAT and POSITION.
Rules:
- One sentence, 125 characters or fewer.
- POSITION 1 is the cover: start with "Cover of {TITLE} by {AUTHOR}",
  then say what the cover shows.
- Other positions: say what the image shows (an interior page,
  sample cards, the box) and its main subject.
- Use TITLE and AUTHOR exactly as given.
- No claims, prices, awards or health benefits.
- Don't start with "Image of" or "Picture of". No emoji, no ALL CAPS.
- If you can't tell what the image shows, return "REVIEW".
Return JSON only: {"alt": "...", "confidence": "high" | "low"}

Validation before a person sees it

  • 1–125 characters, and not just the title.
  • Cover text contains the exact title and the author as stored.
  • No "image of", "picture of", prices or outcome claims, unless the words are part of the title.
  • Valid JSON. "REVIEW" or low confidence goes straight to a person.

Two results, from the 40th anniversary edition

Before

You Can Heal Your Life - image 1

After

Cover of You Can Heal Your Life by Louise Hay, illustrated by Kelly Rae Roberts: a patterned dragonfly on teal watercolor

✓ 121 characters · exact title and author · no claims

Before

You Can Heal Your Life - image 2

After

Page 36 of You Can Heal Your Life: Louise Hay traces self-criticism to one cause, “not loving the self”

✓ 103 characters · says what's on the page

The images are the store's own files. I wrote these two results by hand to show the target; in the workflow they'd come from ChatGPT Enterprise and go through the same checks.

Guardrails

  • Only product data and public images go in. No customer, order or author contract data.
  • Nothing goes live without a named reviewer.
  • Titles, prices and ISBNs are never written by AI; they come from the catalog system.
  • Measure the reviewer edit rate. If more than 10% of results need edits after week 4, fix the prompt before scaling.

Next jobs for the same workflow

  • Meta descriptions in sentence case (the You Can Heal Your Life one is in capitals).
  • First descriptions for the 16 collections, which have none today.
  • Mapping 5,623 tags to a short controlled list, for a person to approve.
  • First drafts of SOPs and weekly notes, checked against the source data.

07 · Cross-sell sets

From the posting

Lead storefront merchandising and conversion rate optimization using customer and performance data to improve product discovery, navigation, promotions, cross-sells, upsells, conversion, and sales.

Many Hay House authors have a book and a deck or journal on the same theme, and the product pages don't connect them. Here are ten pairings from the live catalog, with September 16 prices. Pick an author to see the set.

Ask and It Is Given Paperback$18.99 · 9781401904593View on shop.hayhouse.com ↗

Ask And It Is Given Cards Card deck$24.99 · 9781401910518View on shop.hayhouse.com ↗

The set

Esther and Jerry Hicks

A reader who buys only Ask and It Is Given spends $18.99. The full set brings that order to $43.98.

Where the sets show up

  1. A "Complete the set" block on each product page, filled from the complementary products set in the Search & Discovery app. Dawn-based themes like this one have a block for it.
  2. The same pairing in the cart drawer, one item at most, only when the other item isn't already in the cart.
  3. A "Book and deck sets" collection, linked from Card Decks and from each author page (HH-201).
  4. Optional, with Marketing: a small automatic discount when both items are in the cart.

How I'd measure it

  1. Baseline: four weeks of orders from a Shopify export. Attach rate = orders with both items ÷ orders with either item.
  2. Launch the block on the ten sets first, then extend it to the catalog if it works.
  3. Track block clicks as a GA4 event, plus attach rate, average order value and conversion rate on those product pages.
  4. Read the results after four weeks, or sooner if checkout conversion drops.

Candidates for the next ten come from orders that already contain two titles by the same author.

The first 90 days

What I'd do, in order.

The findings set the order: first the data that every channel reads, then the fixes that need Development, then growth work that depends on both. Each month ends with a short readout to the Director of E-Commerce.

30days

Learn the stores, stop the leaks

  • Get access, list every storefront, app, feed and integration, and who owns each one.
  • Agree the price of record with hayhouse.com, merge the duplicate listings, clean the Format filter and add weights.
  • Start the Monday health check, the weekly report and the AI-assistant channel in GA4.
  • Write the new-title and promotion SOPs with the people who'll use them.

60days

Fix the data model with Development

  • HH-201 (Author entries and filter) and HH-202 (H1s and book structured data) through QA and launch.
  • BISAC codes and subjects into metafields, a controlled tag list, tags off the product page.
  • Alt text in ChatGPT Enterprise, starting with covers of the top 200 sellers.
  • Script and app review with Development and Marketing: the pop-up, tag manager and pixels behind a mobile Lighthouse score of 36.

90days

Grow what's working

  • Book-and-deck sets live and measured, then the first product page tests.
  • Navigation beyond three menu items, collection descriptions and search synonyms in Search & Discovery.
  • Monthly AI-agent check and the redirect map, ready for whatever comes next for hayhouse.com.
  • Quarter review: conversion, feed approvals, AI-referred sessions and catalog-check trend.

hero.alt: Carhartt review — the full review's first screen

sheets.title: The shelf is strong. The data underneath it isn't keeping up.
sheets.html:
Carhartt's storefront has one of the best product-discovery systems in workwear — warmth ratings, deep fit and weight taxonomy, industry shops. The gaps are almost all product-data and merchandising-hygiene problems: empty categories in the New tree during Fall Layering, duplicate facet values, attributes leaking into product names, and a badge slot that hides the one thing a fall shopper needs. All of it is fixable by a site merchandiser in a quarter.

Prepared by Mousa Batarseh as an unsolicited work sample for the Digital Site Merchandiser role. Based only on the public site as it rendered on Sept 15, 2026. No internal data, no Carhartt assets or logos used.

Reviewed
Sept 15, 2026
Surfaces
Home · nav tree (392 category links) · 12 PLPs · PDP · site search · sitemap · robots
Stack seen
SAP Commerce Cloud (Spartacus) · Algolia search · Adobe Dynamic Media · True Fit
Season live
“Stock up on layers” · Fall Sale 25% · Force Cold
Author
Mousa Batarseh, Warren MI

13 findings, each with a captured example, the customer impact, and a fix

2 categories in the New nav tree showing “0 items” mid-September, including Women's New Outerwear

10 / 24 Men's Jackets tiles that show no warmth rating because another badge takes the slot

2× Rugged Flex® and Rain Defender® each listed twice in the Technology facet — one delimiter apart

6 quick wins that need no dev work — content, PIM, and merchandising rules only

Performs well

Keep doing this

Before the fixes: the parts of the digital shelf that are ahead of most apparel sites. These are the systems the findings below should be built on, not replaced.

  • Warmth rating is a real merchandising system

    Chips at the top of jacket PLPs (Warm → Extreme Warmth), “Rated Warm/Warmest” tile badges, a Warmth Rating facet, and “Warmth Rating Earned: Level 1” at the top of every PDP description. One attribute, four surfaces, consistent language. This is the spine of fall merchandising.

  • Taxonomy shops the way tradespeople think

    Fit (Relaxed / Loose / Slim), weight (Lightweight / Midweight / Heavyweight), Big & Tall, Plus, Shop by Industry (Construction, Farm & Ranch, Mechanic, Electrician, Medical), Shop by Warmth Rating. Facet-as-category done right, and it earns long-tail search traffic.

  • Storytelling inside the grid

    “Aisle invader” content tiles sit in the product grid (“Outwork the rain — Shop rainwear”), so seasonal stories run where people are already shopping instead of only in a hero.

  • Sale presentation is honest and scannable

    Original vs. Now ranges on tiles, color-count “+ N” cues, and a 24-up grid with “See 14 more” instead of infinite scroll. Nothing hides the price story.

  • PDP fundamentals are in place

    Detroit Jacket: 4.2★ from 1,322 reviews, 223 Q&A, Regular/Tall size architecture, True Fit sizing, five product images, a “Built to Last” guarantee block. The trust content exists — it just isn't surfaced upstream yet (see F-08).

  • Legacy seasonal URLs are canonicalized

    /c/women-new-spring-jackets and /c/women-new-rain-gear both resolve to the current Women's New Outerwear node. The redirect discipline is there — the destination is the problem (see F-01).

Opportunities

13 findings, in priority order

Ordered by revenue impact against effort. Each one shows exactly what was captured on the live site, why a customer or the business feels it, and the fix I'd ship. Severity: Fix this week This quarter Polish

F-01 Fix this week

Empty categories · Sitemap · Seasonal

Women's New Outerwear shows 0 items in the New nav — during Fall Layering

The “New” menu has a Women's branch. Its outerwear node renders an empty grid, with two legacy URLs redirecting into it. A second empty category (men-insulated-bibs-coveralls) is still in the XML sitemap while the live equivalent lives at a different slug with 8 products. Both pages show search-error copy on a category page.

captured · /c/women-new-outerwear · breadcrumb: Home › New Clothing & Accessories › New Women's Clothes & Gear

WOMEN'S NEW OUTERWEAR — 0 items — No matches found for: "women-new-outerwear" — Check the spelling of the search term you entered.

captured · /c/men-insulated-bibs-coveralls (in Category.xml) vs /c/men-insulated-bib-and-coveralls (in nav)

0 items vs 8 items — same intent, two slugs, one dead.

Impact

Women's is a stated growth segment and this is the newness door for it. Google also has an indexable “0 items” page in the sitemap.

Fix

Assign the current women's outerwear launches to the node today. Then: a weekly “zero-product category” report from the catalog, an empty-state that falls back to the parent category (prototype P-3), 301 the dead slug to the live one, and drop it from Category.xml.

Effort

Hours for the assignment; one sprint for the report and empty-state template.

F-02 Fix this week

Facets · PIM · Search

Facet values are split by punctuation and spelling

On Men's Jackets & Coats the Technology facet lists the same technology twice with a different delimiter. Lining has four names for one taffeta quilt. Fabric has “Polyester” and “100% Polyester.” New & Featured has a typo and carries fabric values that belong in Fabric. Every duplicate halves the count a shopper sees and doubles the clicks to filter.

captured · Technology facet · /c/men-coats-jackets

Rugged Flex- Range of Motion · Rugged Flex: Range of Motion · Rain Defender- Water Repellent · Rain Defender: Water Repellent · Full Swing- Range of Motion · Force: Sweat-Wicking · Storm Defender- Waterproof Breathable · Super Dux- Water Repellent & Wind Resistant · Yukon Extremes- Extreme Warmth

captured · Lining · Fabric · New & Featured

Lining: Taffeta · Quilted Taffeta · Polyester Quilted Taffeta · Quilt · Quilted Flannel  |  Fabric: Polyester · 100% Polyester  |  New & Featured: New · New Colors · Best Seller's · Fall Layering · Lightweight · Duck · Camo · Montana

Impact

Filter abandonment and under-counted technologies on the page where Rugged Flex® and Rain Defender® are the reasons to buy.

Fix

A controlled vocabulary per facet in the PIM (one value, one spelling, “Name: Benefit” format), a bulk normalization pass on the affected attributes, and a monthly facet-value diff so new launches can't reintroduce variants. Prototype P-2 shows the before/after.

Effort

Merchandising + PIM only. No storefront code.

F-03 Fix this week

Badges · PLP · Seasonal

One badge slot per tile — “New” hides the warmth rating on the newest fall jackets

Tiles show exactly one badge. When a jacket is New, Exclusive, Sale, or Steady Rain, its warmth rating disappears from the shelf. On the 24 tiles captured from Men's Jackets & Coats, 10 show no warmth signal — including this season's Montana Ranch Coat, Elkhart, and Fairbanks launches, the products the Fall campaign is pushing.

captured · tile badge images · /c/men-coats-jackets

Montana Rugged Flex® Duck Ranch Coat → ProductBadge_New (no Warmth_Rating) · Elkhart Jacket → ProductBadge_New · Fairbanks Active Jac → ProductBadge_New · Crafted Series ×4 → Exclusive · Gilliam Jacket → none · Monterey → ProductBadge_SteadyRain

Impact

Warmth is the primary decision attribute in Q4; the shelf goes quiet on it for the products with the most marketing behind them.

Fix

Two badge slots: status (New / Exclusive / Sale) top-left, warmth top-right, with a priority rule so nothing stacks past two. Prototype P-1 shows the tile.

Effort

One tile-template change + a badge priority rule.

F-04 This quarter

Product data · Naming · URLs

Attributes are leaking into product names and URLs

A warmth rating that belongs in an attribute is appended to some product names, so it reaches the URL slug, the tile, the title tag, and the feed. Trademark symbols alternate between ® and ™ on the same technology. Women's names carry a “WOMEN'S” prefix inside the women's category; men's don't. The Detroit Jacket has three different names depending on where you meet it.

captured · names and slugs

RUGGED FLEX® DUCK LOOSE FIT CHORE COAT - 1 WARM RATING → /product/106675/rugged-flex-duck-loose-fit-chore-coat---1-warm-rating · YUKON EXTREMES™ INSULATED COVERALL - 4 EXTREME WARMTH RATING · MONTANA RUGGED FLEX® DUCK RANCH COAT vs MONTANA RUGGED FLEX™ DUCK JACKET · YUKON EXTREMES® vs YUKON EXTREMES™

captured · one product, three names

PLP: “Iconic J01 Duck Detroit Jacket” · PDP H1: “Carhartt J01 Men's Iconic Duck Blanket Lined Detroit Jacket | Carhartt” · image alt: “Carhartt Iconic J01 Duck Detroit Jacket”

Impact

Ugly slugs and titles in search results and shopping feeds; inconsistent brand marks; harder product matching for reviews, feeds, and analytics.

Fix

A one-page naming convention (Series · Technology · Fabric · Silhouette; no attributes; ® on the first mention only), a PIM validation that blocks “rating” strings in names, and a cleanup of the affected styles with 301s.

Effort

A day of data work, a template fix for the H1 suffix.

F-05 This quarter

PDP · Cross-sell · Seasonal

The Detroit Jacket PDP recommends “Warm Weather Essentials”

While the homepage says “Stock up on layers that have no off-season,” the flagship fall jacket's second recommendation rail is Force tees, a Sun Defender™ polo, and a short-sleeve logo tee. The first rail (“You May Also Like”) is fine and even cross-sells into bibs. The second one is a seasonal rule that wasn't retired.

captured · /product/103828/iconic-j01-duck-detroit-jacket

YOU MAY ALSO LIKE: Force Phoenix Jacket · Rugged Flex® Duck Berwick Jacket · Washed Duck Active Jac · Washed Duck Insulated Bib Overall  |  WARM WEATHER ESSENTIALS: Force Relaxed T-Shirt · Force Relaxed LS T-Shirt · Force Sun Defender™ Relaxed Logo Polo · Force Sun Defender™ Relaxed LS Logo T-Shirt

Impact

Lost attach rate on the one PDP with the most traffic in the season.

Fix

Retire the rail; replace with a “Complete the layer” rail keyed to warmth rating (base layer → hoodie → this jacket → insulated bib). Put a seasonal expiry date on every manual rec rule. Prototype P-4.

Effort

Merchandising rule change; no code.

F-06 This quarter

Facets · Taxonomy

“Product Type” mixes four dimensions that already have their own facets

On jackets, Product Type offers Duck and Denim (fabric), Fleece and Sherpa (lining), Rain Jackets (protection), Insulated / Lined (lining again), Lightweight (weight), plus the actual silhouettes — Active Jacs, Coats, Softshell. Fabric, Lining, Rain Protection, and Warmth Rating each exist as separate facets, so shoppers see the same choice twice under different names and results don't add up.

captured · Product Type · /c/men-coats-jackets

Insulated / Lined · Rain Jackets · Winter Jackets · Lightweight · Active Jacs · Duck · Denim Jackets · Fleece · Sherpa · Coats · Softshell · Flame-Resistant

Fix

Product Type = silhouette only (Active Jac, Chore Coat, Ranch Coat, Shirt Jac, Vest, Parka, Softshell, Pullover). Fabric, Lining, Rain Protection, and Warmth carry the rest. Re-map values in the PIM; the facet order becomes Warmth → Product Type → Size → Fabric → Technology.

Effort

Attribute mapping; a few days with the data team.

F-07 This quarter

PLP · Social proof

Ratings live on the PDP but never reach the shelf

The Detroit Jacket carries 4.2★ from 1,322 reviews. The PLP tile shows none of it, even though a “Top Rated” sort exists. Shoppers comparing 38 jackets get price, colors, and one badge — not the signal that decides most apparel purchases.

captured · PDP vs PLP tile

PDP: 4.2 out of 5 · 1322 Reviews · 223 Questions  |  PLP tile: name · price range · swatches · one badge · no rating

Fix

Stars + count on tiles (hide under 5 reviews). Prototype P-1.

Effort

Tile template; review data is already indexed for the sort.

F-08 This quarter

Assortment · Tagging · Women's

Fall categories look thin in ways that smell like tagging, not assortment

Men's Lined Sweatshirts & Hoodies holds 3 items during a layering campaign. Women's Jackets & Coats holds 19 vs. 38 for men, and its first two tiles are shirt jacs — which have their own category. Men's Insulated Overalls includes an insulated pant. Either the products are missing, or the attributes that route them into these nodes are.

captured · category counts, Sept 15

/c/men-lined-hoodies → 3 items · /c/women-coats-jackets → 19 items (first tiles: Women's Paxton Quilted Shirt Jac, Women's Highland Shirt Jac) · /c/men-insulated-bib-and-coveralls → 8 items incl. Firm Duck Insulated Pant

Fix

An attribute-coverage audit for the fall nodes: every SKU in the season's buy checked against lining, warmth, silhouette, and gender-category assignment. Fill gaps before Black Friday.

F-09 This quarter

Content · Quick filters · QA

Quick-filter chip groups are mislabeled on some categories

The chip bar on Men's Rain Jackets is titled “Warmth” but contains Cold, Rainy, Cotton Duck, and Lightweight. The same template on Jackets is labeled correctly. It reads like a content block copied between categories without a QA pass.

captured · /c/new-men-rain-jackets

WARMTH — Most Popular · Cold · Rainy · Cotton Duck · Lightweight

Fix

A launch checklist item per category: chip label matches chip set. A content QA pass over the ~40 categories using this component.

F-10 This quarter

Category naming · SEO

URL, title tag, and H1 disagree on what a category is

/c/winter-sale returns a page titled “Limited Time Deals” with an H1 of “Pants & Accessories Sale” (466 items). The insulated-bibs node is “Insulated” in the nav, “Men's Insulated Overalls” as the H1, and “Insulated Bibs & Coveralls - Mens Insulated Bibs & Lined Coveralls for Men” as the title. Shoppers arriving from search see one name, then another.

captured

/c/winter-sale → title “Limited Time Deals” → H1 “PANTS & ACCESSORIES SALE” · /c/men-insulated-bib-and-coveralls → nav “Insulated” → H1 “MEN'S INSULATED OVERALLS” → title “Insulated Bibs & Coveralls - Mens …”

Fix

One name per node, propagated to slug, H1, title, and breadcrumb from the PIM; stop reusing evergreen slugs for rotating promos — give promos their own /c/promo-… nodes with an end date.

F-11 This quarter

Search · Merch rules

Top seasonal queries land on a results grid, not the category

Searching “insulated bibs” returns correct products with Men / Women / Kids chips — good — but no route to the curated Insulated Overalls node, its warmth chips, or its facets. The “Products you may be interested in” block below the results is a fixed set of four styles that doesn't reflect the query.

captured · /search/insulated%20bibs

MEN · WOMEN · KIDS · results grid · PRODUCTS YOU MAY BE INTERESTED IN: Iconic J01 Duck Detroit Jacket · Iconic J140 Firm Duck Active Jac · Paxton Sweatshirt · Iconic R01 Duck Bib Overall

Fix

Search-to-category redirects (or a “Shop the category” banner) for the top 50 category-intent queries, refreshed each season from Algolia analytics; a recommendation block that reflects the query.

F-12 Polish

Sort · Newness

No “Newest” sort on a site that merchandises newness everywhere

Sort offers Relevance, Top Rated, Price ↑↓, Name ↑↓. New is a facet checkbox instead. The New menu, New Colors, Just Added, and “New for …” nodes all exist; the grid can't be ordered by them.

captured · sort options

Relevance · Top Rated · Price Low to High · Price High to Low · Name Ascending · Name Descending

Fix

Add “Newest” (launch date desc). Name sorts are rarely used on apparel and could go.

F-13 Polish

Templates · Structured data · Accessibility

Template details that cost trust with Google and screen readers

Badge images use their file names as alt text — a screen reader hears “Warmth underscore Rating underscore 1” and “ProductBadge underscore New” instead of “Rated Warm.” The PDP H1 includes the “| Carhartt” title suffix. The Product JSON-LD description contains a literal “Description” label and “ ” entities. The category meta description spells the brand's own technology “water-repellant.”

captured

badge alt="Warmth_Rating_1" · alt="ProductBadge_New" · alt="ProductBadge_SteadyRain" · JSON-LD description: "\n\n\nDescription\nWarmth Rating Earned: Level 1 - Warm\n …" · meta: "…insulated, water-repellant jackets…"

Fix

Human-readable alt on badge images (“Rated Warm, level 1”); strip the title suffix from H1; clean the description field before it's serialized; copy fix on the meta.

Method

How this was captured

What I looked at
  • Homepage, the full navigation tree (392 unique /c/ links), and Category.xml from the sitemap index.
  • 12 category pages including Men's Jackets & Coats (facets, sort, 24 tiles, badges), Women's Jackets & Coats, Men's Rain, Lined Hoodies, Insulated Overalls, Force, New Women's, Low Stock, Winter Sale.
  • One PDP end to end (Iconic J01 Duck Detroit Jacket): H1, JSON-LD, images, size architecture, recommendation rails.
  • Site search for a top seasonal query (“insulated bibs”).
  • robots.txt (Algolia crawler allowed, search and query parameters disallowed).
Limits
  • Public site only, one day, one region (US), desktop and narrow viewports. No analytics, no inventory, no launch calendar — so counts like “3 items” are observations, not verdicts.
  • “Not shown on tile” means the badge slot was taken; the product almost certainly has a warmth rating in the data.
  • Every quote in the findings is verbatim text or attribute values as rendered. Nothing was fetched from Carhartt's CDN and no brand assets are reproduced.

sheets.html:
Start from what's already right

The store has the hard things in place: trust, a clean photo look, and real part numbers. The fixes below are about getting more buyers to find and believe each listing.

Trust

100% positive feedback across 2.3K items sold, 30-day returns with the seller paying return shipping, and 24-hour handling.

A consistent photo look

White sweep, the ICR mark in the corner, and a close-up of the nameplate — the label shot is exactly what a technician checks first.

Real identifiers

Titles lead with brand and model and carry the controller; parts carry the manufacturer part number and an MPN item specific.

Webstore structured data

Product pages publish Product schema with MPN, price, stock, RefurbishedCondition, and a 30-day return policy — a solid SEO foundation.

Local fulfillment

Listings ship from Warren (the pendant I checked quoted 2–4 day delivery), and the webstore offers same-day shipping on in-stock parts ordered by 1 PM.

12 findings

What I'd fix first

Everything below was captured from the live eBay store and icrservices.com on September 15, 2026. Each finding has the evidence, why it costs sales, and the fix. Fixes marked with a tool link are built further down this page.

01 High

eBay · item 132708949075

“Tested, warranty” is in the title but nowhere in the listing

ABB TPU2 teach pendant — US $3,499.95 or Best Offer Title:

ABB TPU2-EX TEACH PENDANT 3HNE00442-1 **TESTED WARRANTY**

Condition: Seller refurbished Description: weight, box size, payment and shipping terms — no test details, no warranty term, and all items are sold as used unless otherwise stated

A buyer spending $3,500 on a pendant wants proof it works and to know what the warranty covers. When the title, the condition, and the description say three different things, the buyer either messages and waits, or buys elsewhere — and a sale made on a mismatch can come back as “not as described.”

Fix

One description template for every tested item: what was tested and on which stand, the warranty length, and what's in the box — with the condition wording matching the title. See the rewritten listing →

02 High

eBay · FANUC titles

One robot family, seven spellings

R-2000 family across the 59 live titlesR2000IB · R2000iB · R-2000IB · R-2000IC · R2000IC · R2000iC · and once, FANUC's own

R-2000iB

(on a wrist listing) Controllers: R30IA · R30iA · R30IB · R30IB+ · R30IB Plus · R30IB PLUS — FANUC's own R-30iA / R-30iB Plus never appears

Technicians search the way the nameplate or the manual reads, and plenty type it without the hyphen. A listing shouldn't depend on the search engine guessing that “R-2000iB” and “R2000iB” are the same robot. Inconsistent naming also makes the store look like it was listed by five different people.

Fix

A naming convention: Brand + official model + type + official controller, then the no-hyphen variant where space allows (e.g. FANUC R-2000iB/210F Industrial Robot Arm w/ R-30iA Controller R2000iB 210F). Linter + rewrites →

03 Medium

eBay · 42 of 59 titles

Serial numbers are using space that buyers' search words should get

Longest example — 32 characters of an 80-character title

MOTOMAN UP6 ROBOT WITH XRC CONTROLLER SN: (R) S2M003-1-1 (C) S1M544-1-2

Nobody searches a serial number before they know it exists. Meanwhile the words buyers do type — “industrial robot arm,” “Yaskawa” for Motoman, payload, application — are missing. The serial already sits in the nameplate photo, which is the right place for it.

Fix

Move serials to an item specific and the label photo; spend the space on search terms. The UP6 becomes Yaskawa Motoman UP6 Industrial Robot Arm w/ XRC Controller UP-6 6-Axis (70/80).

04 Medium

eBay · 14 titles, 51 all-caps

Asterisks and all caps read as noise

Across the 59 titles**TESTED WARRANTY** ×10 · *REFURBISHED* ×4 · 51 of 59 titles written almost entirely in capitals

Symbols don't match any search and cost characters. “Refurbished” already exists as eBay's condition filter, so it earns its place in the title only as a plain word. Mixed case with correct model spelling (R-30iB, not R30IB) is easier to scan in a results page full of shouting titles.

Fix

Plain words (“Tested with Warranty”, “Refurbished”), brand-first, official capitalization. The linter below flags every case automatically.

05 High

eBay · items 167252727995, 167792818349, 168588511029

Part numbers disagree inside the same title

Allen-Bradley PowerFlex 700 — both spellings are in one title

ALLEN BRADLEY POWERFLEX 700 125HP 20B C 170 A 0 AYANC0 20BC170A0AYNANC0

spaced version joined: 20BC170A0AY_ANC0 ≠ 20BC170A0AYNANC0 (one “N” missing) FANUC R-2000iB wrist — $14,249.95… WRIST A290-7329-T501**TESTED WARRANTY** (no space: the part number runs into the asterisks) FANUC R-2000iB/210F… W/ R30iA Controller R30iA SN: F-154664 (controller repeated)

Part-number buyers search the exact catalog string from their nameplate. One dropped character is a missed match — and a tech comparing the title to the drive in front of them will hesitate on a $9,499.95 purchase.

Fix

Copy part numbers from the label photo, not from memory, keep a space on both sides, and run a QA check before publishing. The linter flags repeated words, glued part numbers, and spaced-vs-joined part numbers that don't match.

06 Medium

eBay · item specifics

Item specifics stop at Brand, MPN, UPC

ABB TPU2 teach pendant — every item specific on the listingBrand: ABB · MPN: 3HNE00442-1 · UPC: Does not apply

Item specifics drive eBay's search filters and the “compatible with” questions buyers ask. With three fields, the listing can't show up when a buyer filters by type, model, or controller.

Fix

A specifics set per category (teach pendants, servo motors, drives, robots) filled from the label and the test record: Model, Type, Revision, Compatible Controller, Cable, Serial, Country of Manufacture, Warranty. Example →

07 Medium

eBay · photos

3 photos of 24 — and none of the pendant powered on

ABB TPU2 teach pendant — photo set1. front on sweep (display has glare) 2. three-quarter angle 3. nameplate missing: powered-on screen on the test stand · back · connector end · cable length · keypad/joystick close-ups · wear

For a tested electronic part, a photo of it booted on ICR's test stand is the most persuasive image in the listing — it proves the “tested” claim without a word. More angles also answer questions before buyers have to ask.

Fix

A 12-shot standard for parts, done the same way every time. Checklist →

08 Low

eBay · image editing

The white sweep photographs light gray

Background sampled from photo 1 (median RGB)bottom-right 234, 238, 238 · bottom-left 236, 241, 243 · target 255, 255, 255

Next to competitors' pure-white thumbnails, a gray, slightly cool background looks dimmer in search results. It's a two-step fix that can be batched across every photo.

Fix

White-balance off the sweep, then set the white point — shadows kept, product untouched. Saved as a Photoshop action or a script so every set gets the same edit. Before/after →

09 Medium

eBay · label vs title

The nameplate says more than the title

Label in photo 3 vs the titleLabel:

TPU2-EX · Art.no: 3HNE 00442-1/05

Title: 3HNE00442-1 (revision dropped; label's spaced form not included)

A technician replacing a failed unit often matches the full article number including the revision, and ABB prints it with a space — so both forms get typed into search.

Fix

Title carries 3HNE00442-1/05 and 3HNE 00442-1; revision goes into item specifics too.

10 Growth

eBay · assortment

The store is mostly whole robots — parts are the everyday buy

59 active listings48 complete robots ($6,999.95 – $36,080.95) 11 parts: 4 servo motors · 4 wrists · 1 teach pendant · 1 rectifier · 1 drive icrservices.com lists a refurbished FANUC P-155 wrist (EO-0833-010)

IN STOCK

at $8,995.95 — not on eBay; the ICR homepage cites 20,000 SKUs in its equipment catalogue

Maintenance teams buy pendants, motors, amplifiers, boards and cables every week; whole robots sell a few times a year. A robot that isn't moving can become a dozen listings once it's pulled and disassembled — which is exactly the work this role describes.

Fix

A part-out line for slow-moving robots, plus cross-listing in-stock refurbished parts from the webstore to eBay. Part-out planner →

11 Medium

icrservices.com · product page

Webstore pages lead with the part number only

/catalogue/fanuc-eo-0833-010<title>

FANUC - EO-0833-010 | ICR

(no product name) H1: FANUC - EO-0833-010 Meta description: P–155 Wrist Assembly (en dash; the Series field says P-155) Buy panel: Test Method · Test: (blank) · 1 product photo

Someone searching “FANUC P-155 wrist” doesn't see those words in the page title, and a typed hyphen doesn't match an en dash. The empty test field looks unfinished on a $9,000 item — the Product schema underneath is already excellent, so this is copy, not code.

Fix

Title: FANUC P-155 Wrist Assembly EO-0833-010, Refurbished | ICR. Description of ~150 characters with condition, test, warranty and same-day shipping. Fill the test method or hide the field when empty.

12 Low

eBay · store followers

38 followers after 2.3K sales

Store header100% positive · 2.3K items sold · 38 followers

Repeat industrial buyers are the best buyers, and followers see new listings. Almost none of the people who already bought have saved the store.

Fix

A packing-slip insert with a QR code to save the seller and a link to ICR's repair and buyback programs — cheap, and it turns one-time buyers into a channel.

Tool · Titles

A title linter, run on all 59 live listings

I copied every active title from the store and wrote a checker for the problems in findings 2–5. It runs in your browser. The same rules sit behind the title builder, so new listings pass before they go live.

sheets.title: Website experience, examined.
sheets.html:
An evaluation of DiaMedical’s website, with a detailed review of Hospital Beds & Stretchers. Strengths, opportunities, and working examples grounded in recorded evidence.

Prepared by Mousa Batarseh for the Marketing & eCommerce Coordinator interview.

20 sampled pages and states · 6 product pages · Observed September 9, 2026

The story, from problem to proposal

See the problem before trying the fix.

Each path begins with a dated observation. The working proposal then holds the sample constant, makes one change, and checks the result.

  1. Quote labels disagree.

    The saved comparison shows $0.00 and Add To Cart; the product pages describe a quote. The proposal uses one quote state across four views, then runs three QA checks.

    Read the problem Try the quote rule

  2. A matching capacity is missing from the filter.

    Stryker’s product page states 500 lb, but it is absent from the recorded 500 lbs results. The proposal tests a normalized capacity value within six local records.

    Read the problem Try the filter change

  3. Product information needs to support discovery.

    Start with the card decision-support finding. Then explore a proposed search model: add aliases, compare completeness and ranking, inspect every scoring reason, and reset. This is not a measured production search defect.

    Read the finding Try scoring and QA

These are three working demonstrations, not a claim that every finding has an implemented fix. Other findings include a recommendation and a validation plan.

01 · What I was asked to do

Review the experience.
Go deeper on the products.

I was asked to identify what works well and suggest improvements across DiaMedical’s website. The assignment then asks for a closer review of Hospital Beds & Stretchers: how products are presented, how filters work, and how useful the content is. Search, metadata, and SEO provide additional areas to consider.

I organized the response around one purchase a real buyer would make:

“I need a reconditioned bed rated for 500 lb. Which ones, and what will they cost?”

It is a question the catalog can answer. Fourteen products in Hospital Beds & Stretchers state 500 lb or more and are listed as reconditioned. The filters as they stand today reach eleven of them, because three carry no capacity or condition value the facets can read; and none of the fourteen shows a price, so the answer to the second half is a phone call. Following that one question is what produced the strengths and the opportunities in this review.

02 · The problem I investigated

Useful information.
Moments of uncertainty.

DiaMedical already provides product discovery, educational guidance, detailed specifications, and procurement support. I examined how those pieces agree when a customer moves between them.

Read the five strengths

The clearest example is the quote journey. In the captured comparison, Vantage and Stryker S3 With Scale displayed $0.00 and Add To Cart. Their product pages displayed Call for Price and Add To Quote.

The labels disagree. That could make the next step unclear, but its effect on customers still needs a usability check. Other findings include repeated specifications that conflict and a product missing from the tested capacity filter despite matching its stated capacity.

My question is how to make the information more consistent while preserving the useful tools and content already there.

Read the observation and proposed response

03 · What I am doing here

Make the reasoning
something you can follow.

I explain five strengths and nineteen opportunities — twelve from the September 9 walkthrough and seven from a fuller crawl of the category and site on September 10. Each finding connects a public observation to a proposed response and a way to check it. The working examples carry that reasoning into the same customer task.

  1. 01Pathfinder

    Understand

    Choose a buyer task, such as finding a bed for a simulation space.

    A starting point
  2. 02Product Discovery

    Find

    Narrow the six-product sample and compare the details behind a selection.

    An explained shortlist
  3. 03Working examples

    Improve

    Try a proposed quote rule, capacity mapping, or search alias.

    One recorded change
  4. 04Checks & scoring

    Validate

    Repeat the task and inspect what changed and what still needs approval.

    A result to inspect

The useful connection: a customer-facing problem becomes a specific catalog, content, or interface task, with evidence and an expected result attached.

04 · How I did it

Observe. Record.
Explain. Test.

The review starts with public evidence. The interactive examples use a local sample built from those observations.

Inspect all 20 samples

  1. 01

    Inspect the experience.

    I moved from the wider website into Hospital Beds & Stretchers, then followed selected products through product pages, filtering, and comparison.

  2. 02

    Keep an evidence record.

    I retained public URLs, screenshots, page text, product details, and sampled metadata. Each sample has an observation date and links back to its saved evidence.

  3. 03

    Explain the finding.

    I separated what I observed from why it might matter, what I would change, and how I would check it. I included strengths as well as opportunities.

  4. 04

    Build a focused example.

    I used the six product records to demonstrate selected ideas. Proposed aliases and display rules stay separate from the captured source information.

  5. 05

    Repeat the same task.

    I held the sample and rules constant, made one local change, and compared the result. Conflicting specifications remain open for confirmation.

Where the samples came from

20 pages and states.
Six deliberately chosen products.

The products cover a simulation bed, a reconditioned bed, two stretcher types, a configurable homecare bed, and a low bed. This exposes different content and pricing experiences. It is a curated sample of the reviewed experience.

Wider website pages
09
Category routes
03
Product pages
06
Filter & comparison states
02

These counts describe inspected pages and states, not unique inventory. Evidence was observed September 9 in America/Detroit; the register was assembled September 10. Exact screenshot times were not recorded.

05 · How the numbers are made

Three questions.
Three separate answers.

The numbers help explain the demonstration. Each answers a different question.

Inspect every scoring reason

How complete is this record?

0–100 Record completeness combines six weighted field checks: identity 25%, taxonomy 25%, content 20%, SEO 15%, merchandising 10%, and provenance 5%.

Example: applying three suggested Vantage aliases raises local completeness from 75 to 80. It adds merchandising credit; it does not verify the specifications.

Why did this product match?

Ranking points

Search adds points for matching fields such as SKU, title, alias, category, and use case. The page lists the reason for each contribution and shows the product’s position in the sample.

For “simulation bed”, those aliases add 240 points: 290 becomes 530, moving Vantage from second to first in this six-record example.

Did the local change pass its checks?

Pass / open

The quote example checks the comparison label, agreement across all four demonstrated views, and whether a product with a published price keeps that price unchanged.

Applying the quote rule changes the result from 1 of 3 to 3 of 3. This is a local validation result; approval and production testing are still separate steps.

How to read this work

The source, the idea,
and the next check.

The website makes each stage visible so a reviewer can assess the reasoning.

Observed
What appeared on a dated public page or interaction state.
Interpretation
Why that observation may affect a customer’s decision.
Proposed
The change I would consider, including a working local example.
To validate
The check, approved product information, or team confirmation still needed.

How the website itself was built

I built the review as a React and TypeScript website using Vite. Saved evidence and structured sample records support the findings, product comparison, and scoring examples. Browser state holds local selections and drafts; CSV and JSON exports make that work inspectable.

The quote, capacity, and alias controls run against the local sample. The website has no connection to DiaMedical’s internal catalog or analytics. Public observations, proposed changes, and calculated local results remain separate.

Ready to explore

Follow one example.
Then choose your own path.

This review follows the Commerce Intelligence Lab, applying its scoring and QA-loop approach to selected proposals. The walkthrough explains each page and gives you one thing to try. You can go back, hide the instructions, or finish whenever you are ready.

01 What I observed

The homepage uses real simulation and equipment imagery for Vantage beds, loaded crash carts, diagnostic equipment, manikins and lab furnishings. At the tested mobile width, the Vantage campaign becomes a full-width lead card, followed by smaller product cards.

The judgment · a strength to keep

The imagery introduces the storefront.

A homepage should help visitors understand what a business offers and find a useful starting point. The recorded DiaMedical homepage does this through recognizable equipment, teaching environments, and direct shopping actions. A visitor can see the kind of products being offered before opening an individual product page. That is why this finding is a strength.

The recommendation here is to retain that equipment context and its working links. Whether a visitor who does not know a product name can find a planning route is a different question. That is covered in the related opportunity, with its own evidence and working proposal.

sheets.html:
“I need a reconditioned bed rated for 500 lb. Which ones, and what will they cost?” I carried that purchase through the category review, the product sample and every check below.

01 · Understand the task

Start with a customer question.

Pathfinder · A local starting point using the six reviewed products.

Observed on the public website

A useful foundation.
A clearer decision layer.

I found category navigation, specification filters, comparison, detailed product pages and quote options already in place. I would preserve that depth and make the pieces agree when a customer narrows a selection or compares equipment.

30 Parent category

21 Hospital Beds

12 Stretchers Public route counts, reviewed Sep 9, 2026. Categories overlap; these are not an additive inventory total.

Make the quote step clear.

What I observed
The Vantage and Stryker S3 comparison shows $0.00 and Add To Cart. Their product pages say Call for Price and Add To Quote; the comparison action opens a quick view with Add To Quote.
Why it matters
A customer could expect a zero-price purchase before encountering a quote step. The labels disagree; their effect on behavior still needs testing.
What I would do
I would confirm the pricing status and use the same approved label and action across cards, comparison, quick view and product details.
How I would check
Repeat the same task with both quote products and a separately checked priced product. Verify labels, actions and configuration context on each surface.

Inspect the evidence Test quote consistency

Make filtering agree with the product facts.

What I observed
In the September 9 capture, Hospital Beds lists 21 products, including Stryker S3 With Scale. Selecting “500 lbs” leaves six results and removes that bed. Its product page lists “Weight Capacity: 500 lb (227 kg).”
Why it matters
A shopper using this filter could miss a bed whose own page lists the selected capacity. The page separately lists the bed’s own weight as 570 lb; that is not its weight capacity. I have not inspected the system behind the mismatch.
What I would do
I would ask the catalog owner to confirm the exact model and its approved capacity, then make the product-page value and the value used by the filter agree. I would preserve the existing filters and Clear All control.
How I would check
After confirmation, select “500 lbs” again and check that Stryker appears, other results remain appropriate, and refresh and Clear All work. The local demonstration uses a different group of six products: it moves from one match, HC107, to two, HC107 and Stryker. The public result count after a real correction is unknown.

Inspect the evidence Inspect the capacity check

Keep an unanswered question visible.

What I observed
Amstar highlights and specifications give different length and height values. Durastar sections disagree on positioning angle, and AllCare has conflicting width and maximum-height wording.
Why it matters
Someone comparing equipment or planning space needs to know which value applies to the exact configuration.
What I would do
I would retain both values, their source sections and a question for the product owner. A populated field or higher completeness score would not resolve the conflict.
How I would check
Check the repeated values against an approved model-specific source. Until the conflict is resolved, leave the affected comparison field marked Not confirmed.

Inspect the evidence

The working comparison demonstrates a proposed interface using six reviewed public products. It does not replace the source catalog or resolve unverified specifications.
