sheets.title: Recommendations you can click.
sheets.html:
Category filters, a product template and a search box rebuilt from the public Hospital Beds & Stretchers products. The current experience and the proposal sit side by side.

Working prototypes · built from the public category

Three recommendations you can use, not read.

Each prototype rebuilds one part of the Hospital Beds & Stretchers journey with the products DiaMedical already publishes — 33 product pages captured on September 10, 2026 · America/Detroit, plus the one link that no longer resolves. The current experience sits beside the proposal so the difference is inspectable, not asserted.

Local demonstration only. Product names, images, prices and specifications are the public values as captured; nothing on diamedicalusa.com was changed, and no order, quote or search request leaves this page. Corrected filter values are proposals from product-page text and need the catalog owner’s confirmation before any real change.

01 · Category page and filters

Every card answers the buyer’s first three questions

Today 27 of 30 cards show no price and no next step, and eight products carry no brand, type or capacity value, so the filters cannot reach them. The proposal fills the values from the product pages and puts the quote step on the card.

22 of 30products the Brand filter can reach todayOpen the prototype

02 · Product page template

One shape for every bed and stretcher

Tab counts run from 1 to 5 across the 33 pages and the breadcrumb skips the category on all of them. The template keeps the depth the good pages already have and makes the quote step, key facts and category path consistent.

7 of 33product pages with two tabs or fewerOpen the prototype

03 · Search with recovery

A misspelt query still finds the bed

“hosptial bed” returns nothing on the live site and the empty state offers no suggestion. This search reads typos, applies a short synonym list and explains every match.

0results for “hosptial bed” on the live siteOpen the prototype

How the prototypes were built

Server-rendered HTML fetched with a self-identifying audit user agent (CommerceIntelligenceLab-Audit/1.0), 1.5 s between requests; rendered checks in Chrome; PageSpeed Insights run in the browser on 2026-09-10 08:53 EDT. The category’s three routes were read as served: the parent lists 30 products, Hospital Beds 21, Stretchers 12; the union is 34 distinct products because assignment differs by route. Every filter page under the category was fetched so each product’s current filter values are the ones the storefront actually holds, not guesses. Product-page specifications were read for capacity and dimensions. Nothing was inferred from analytics, because none were available.

Choose the recommendations worth discussing, arrange the next steps, and keep the evidence alongside the work.

03findings selected

Your selections and notes stay in this browser. Exports download locally. Ordering, effort, and ownership are proposed for discussion.

  1. Comparison pricing conflicts with the quote journey

    Proposed stage
    First
    Owner
    Catalog + eCommerce
    Effort
    Medium

    Confirm which products have a listed price, a price range, or require a quote. Use that approved status consistently in cards, comparison, quick view, and product details. Document the expected label and action on each surface. A zero value alone should not determine whether a product requires a quote.

    Evidence, validation & acceptance

    Observed on the public site

    The Vantage and Stryker S3 With Scale comparison shows $0.00 and Add To Cart for both. Their full product pages show Call for Price and Add To Quote. The comparison CTA opened a quick view with Add To Quote.

    Observed: 2026-09-09 America/Detroit

    Open source page Inspect captured evidence

    How to validate

    Repeat the comparison with the two confirmed quote products and a separately checked priced product. Quote labels and actions should agree across the pages, while the priced product retains its correct price and configuration behavior. Confirm the source pricing status with the catalog and web teams before implementation.

    Acceptance criteria

    • No quote-only product displays $0.00 or an Add To Cart label; priced products retain verified prices and configuration context.

  2. Resolve contradictory specifications at the source

    Proposed stage
    First
    Owner
    Catalog + eCommerce
    Effort
    Medium

    Record both values, their source sections, the exact product/configuration, and a question for the product owner. Resolve the difference against an approved source, then use the approved value consistently. Until then, comparisons should display Not confirmed.

    Evidence, validation & acceptance

    Observed on the public site

    Amstar highlights list 84.5″ length and 23″–35″ height, while Specifications list 83″ length and 21″–33.5″ height. Durastar highlights say ±16° Trendelenburg while Description says 18° maximum. AllCare's copy offers height "up to 30″" while its specifications give the Hi-Lo setting as 3.6″–25″, and its expandable width is punctuated "35″, 39, – 42″".

    Observed: 2026-09-09 America/Detroit

    Open source page Inspect captured evidence

    How to validate

    Check each repeated measurement against the approved source and configuration. Any remaining differences should be explained or left open. A completeness score cannot establish that a measurement is correct, even when every field is populated.

    Acceptance criteria

    • All repeated measurements agree with an approved source or explain configuration differences. Unresolved dimensions remain Not confirmed in the prototype.

  3. Name the mobile navigation button for assistive technology

    Proposed stage
    First
    Owner
    Web development
    Effort
    Small

    Give the control a meaningful accessible name and include its state, keyboard activation, close behavior, and focus return in a focused development ticket.

    Evidence, validation & acceptance

    Observed on the public site

    At 390×844 the visible hamburger control appears in the accessibility tree as an unnamed button. The control (.header-sidebar-toggle) contains an SVG icon and carries no aria-label, no title and no visible text. Expanding it opens the navigation drawer.

    Observed: 2026-09-09 America/Detroit

    Open source page Inspect captured evidence

    How to validate

    Confirm that assistive technology announces the name and state, and that keyboard users can open and close the drawer with focus returning to the control. This checks the observed issue; a full accessibility audit would cover more of the site.

    Acceptance criteria

    • The button is announced with a meaningful name.
    • The expanded state follows the visible drawer.
    • Keyboard activation, Escape/close and return of focus are tested with the drawer.

Start again with the suggested shortlist.

Decide what success would mean.

No analytics service is connected to this review. Baselines are unknown. These definitions describe a proposed measurement plan, with no assumed improvement or revenue effect.

Discovery to product detail

Unique eligible sessions that reach a product detail page from the reviewed category, divided by unique eligible sessions that view that category.

Keep the attribution window and category scope fixed. Exclude internal and automated traffic consistently.

Proposed events

category_viewedproduct_detail_viewed

Product detail to comparison

Unique eligible sessions that open a comparison containing at least two products after viewing a product detail page, divided by unique eligible sessions that view a product detail page in the reviewed category.

Use the same cohort and reporting window. Check selection persistence and product identifiers; comparison use alone does not prove a better buying decision.

Proposed events

product_detail_viewedcomparison_viewed

Comparison to quote action

Unique eligible sessions that click a quote action after a comparison, divided by unique eligible sessions that view a comparison containing at least two products.

Record product identifiers and the page of origin. A quote click indicates intent; it does not establish a submitted lead.

Proposed events

comparison_viewedquote_action_clicked

Instrumentation, consent requirements, event deduplication, and the reporting window would need agreement before a baseline could be measured. No visitor tracking is added by this plan.

How the evidence was collected

A focused sample.
A visible boundary.

The review moves from the wider website into Hospital Beds & Stretchers, then follows selected products through filtering, comparison, and the next action.

36 screenshots appear in this register, including 4 dated follow-up captures. The project retains 39 original screenshots plus 4 follow-up captures, including additional views used by individual findings.

Why these six products?

Vantage, Stryker S3 With Scale, Amstar, Durastar, HomeCare, and AllCare cover a simulation bed, a reconditioned bed, two stretcher types, a configurable homecare bed, and a low bed. Their pages expose different specifications, conditions, and pricing states.

This is a curated sample, not a random or representative sample of the full catalog. Conflicting specifications remain open for confirmation.

What was inspected?

Nine website pages, three category routes, six product pages, a capacity-filter state, and a two-product comparison state. The review covered navigation, product content, existing filters, comparison, mobile presentation, and sampled metadata.

The original desktop and mobile inspections used 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 CSS viewports. A screenshot’s encoded dimensions may differ from its browser viewport. The catalog follow-up uses focused card captures; its separate record preserves the viewport and card bounds for each image.

The 20 original sample observation dates are September 9, 2026 in America/Detroit, with day precision. Individual times for those original screenshots were not recorded.

The September 10 catalog follow-up is separate: each new image records its own observation date and exact capture time in America/Detroit and UTC. It adds evidence to two existing samples without changing their September 9 dates or the other sample records.

What does this review leave open?

Backend configuration, internal search and conversion analytics, manufacturer approval, and business priorities require confirmation. No account authentication or form, quote, or order submission was performed.

Category counts can overlap. Missing fields in a collected sample do not prove missing data in DiaMedical’s systems. Proposed metadata, aliases, summaries, and other local enrichment should remain separate from captured source facts.

What already works

Build on a useful foundation.

DiaMedical already connects equipment, educational guidance, and procurement support. I would keep these strengths visible as the experience develops.

01 Keep the education-led product storytelling

The homepage uses real simulation and equipment imagery for Vantage beds, loaded crash carts, diagnostic equipment, manikins and lab furnishings. At the tested mobile width, the Vantage campaign becomes a full-width lead card, followed by smaller product cards.

What I would preserve. Preserve the strong product imagery and direct product/category links when refining the shopping experience.

Inspect the evidence

02 Educational guidance already connects needs to equipment

The Sim Lab Startup Guide explains equipment groups such as patient-care manikins, bed suites, headwalls and infusion pumps, and supplies product links. The Virtual Learning Center groups product knowledge, simulation innovation and educational tips.

What I would preserve. Use this existing expertise as the foundation for task-based guidance and connect relevant guide sections to product decisions.

Inspect the evidence

03 Procurement and support routes are already present

The primary navigation exposes catalog requests and White Glove Delivery & Installation. The resources page offers seven labeled PDF catalog links plus a printed-catalog request. The delivery page lists assembly, headwalls, privacy systems, inventory/testing and scheduling, with a service-request link. Phone, email and chat support are visibly available.

What I would preserve. Carry these practical procurement aids into category and product decision points, including the distinction between buying equipment and arranging installation.

Inspect the evidence

04 Useful discovery tools are already present

The parent category displays 30 products, Hospital Beds 21 and Stretchers 12. Hospital Beds exposes brand, condition, positions and capacity facets. Selecting 500 lbs returns 6 products and exposes Clear All with a filter-specific URL.

What I would preserve. Preserve category links, sort, capacity/condition filters, result count and reset behavior while refining their labels and visual hierarchy.

Inspect the evidence

05 Keep the practical depth in product pages

Vantage has Description, Specifications, Media & PDFs and Warranty tabs, with capacity, patient surface and dimensions in Specifications. Stryker S3 includes brochure/specification links. HomeCare exposes color, side rail, mattress and size selections. The inspected quote-only PDPs explicitly describe pricing and longer lead times.

What I would preserve. Retain this depth, add a concise facts strip near the product title, and preserve downloadable source links and configuration requirements.

sheets.title: Website experience, examined.
sheets.html:
An evaluation of DiaMedical’s website, with a detailed review of Hospital Beds & Stretchers. Strengths, opportunities, and working examples grounded in recorded evidence.

Prepared by Mousa Batarseh for the Marketing & eCommerce Coordinator interview.

20 sampled pages and states · 6 product pages · Observed September 9, 2026

The story, from problem to proposal

See the problem before trying the fix.

Each path begins with a dated observation. The working proposal then holds the sample constant, makes one change, and checks the result.

  1. Quote labels disagree.

    The saved comparison shows $0.00 and Add To Cart; the product pages describe a quote. The proposal uses one quote state across four views, then runs three QA checks.

    Read the problem Try the quote rule

  2. A matching capacity is missing from the filter.

    Stryker’s product page states 500 lb, but it is absent from the recorded 500 lbs results. The proposal tests a normalized capacity value within six local records.

    Read the problem Try the filter change

  3. Product information needs to support discovery.

    Start with the card decision-support finding. Then explore a proposed search model: add aliases, compare completeness and ranking, inspect every scoring reason, and reset. This is not a measured production search defect.

    Read the finding Try scoring and QA

These are three working demonstrations, not a claim that every finding has an implemented fix. Other findings include a recommendation and a validation plan.

01 · What I was asked to do

Review the experience.
Go deeper on the products.

I was asked to identify what works well and suggest improvements across DiaMedical’s website. The assignment then asks for a closer review of Hospital Beds & Stretchers: how products are presented, how filters work, and how useful the content is. Search, metadata, and SEO provide additional areas to consider.

I organized the response around one purchase a real buyer would make:

“I need a reconditioned bed rated for 500 lb. Which ones, and what will they cost?”

It is a question the catalog can answer. Fourteen products in Hospital Beds & Stretchers state 500 lb or more and are listed as reconditioned. The filters as they stand today reach eleven of them, because three carry no capacity or condition value the facets can read; and none of the fourteen shows a price, so the answer to the second half is a phone call. Following that one question is what produced the strengths and the opportunities in this review.

02 · The problem I investigated

Useful information.
Moments of uncertainty.

DiaMedical already provides product discovery, educational guidance, detailed specifications, and procurement support. I examined how those pieces agree when a customer moves between them.

Read the five strengths

The clearest example is the quote journey. In the captured comparison, Vantage and Stryker S3 With Scale displayed $0.00 and Add To Cart. Their product pages displayed Call for Price and Add To Quote.

The labels disagree. That could make the next step unclear, but its effect on customers still needs a usability check. Other findings include repeated specifications that conflict and a product missing from the tested capacity filter despite matching its stated capacity.

My question is how to make the information more consistent while preserving the useful tools and content already there.

Read the observation and proposed response

03 · What I am doing here

Make the reasoning
something you can follow.

I explain five strengths and nineteen opportunities — twelve from the September 9 walkthrough and seven from a fuller crawl of the category and site on September 10. Each finding connects a public observation to a proposed response and a way to check it. The working examples carry that reasoning into the same customer task.

The useful connection: a customer-facing problem becomes a specific catalog, content, or interface task, with evidence and an expected result attached.

04 · How I did it

Observe. Record.
Explain. Test.

The review starts with public evidence. The interactive examples use a local sample built from those observations.

Inspect all 20 samples

  1. 01

    Inspect the experience.

    I moved from the wider website into Hospital Beds & Stretchers, then followed selected products through product pages, filtering, and comparison.

  2. 02

    Keep an evidence record.

    I retained public URLs, screenshots, page text, product details, and sampled metadata. Each sample has an observation date and links back to its saved evidence.

  3. 03

    Explain the finding.

    I separated what I observed from why it might matter, what I would change, and how I would check it. I included strengths as well as opportunities.

  4. 04

    Build a focused example.

    I used the six product records to demonstrate selected ideas. Proposed aliases and display rules stay separate from the captured source information.

  5. 05

    Repeat the same task.

    I held the sample and rules constant, made one local change, and compared the result. Conflicting specifications remain open for confirmation.

Where the samples came from

20 pages and states.
Six deliberately chosen products.

The products cover a simulation bed, a reconditioned bed, two stretcher types, a configurable homecare bed, and a low bed. This exposes different content and pricing experiences. It is a curated sample of the reviewed experience.

05 · How the numbers are made

Three questions.
Three separate answers.

The numbers help explain the demonstration. Each answers a different question.

Inspect every scoring reason

How complete is this record?

0–100 Record completeness combines six weighted field checks: identity 25%, taxonomy 25%, content 20%, SEO 15%, merchandising 10%, and provenance 5%.

Example: applying three suggested Vantage aliases raises local completeness from 75 to 80. It adds merchandising credit; it does not verify the specifications.

Why did this product match?

Ranking points

Search adds points for matching fields such as SKU, title, alias, category, and use case. The page lists the reason for each contribution and shows the product’s position in the sample.

For “simulation bed”, those aliases add 240 points: 290 becomes 530, moving Vantage from second to first in this six-record example.

Did the local change pass its checks?

Pass / open

The quote example checks the comparison label, agreement across all four demonstrated views, and whether a product with a published price keeps that price unchanged.

Applying the quote rule changes the result from 1 of 3 to 3 of 3. This is a local validation result; approval and production testing are still separate steps.

The source, the idea,
and the next check.

How the website itself was built

I built the review as a React and TypeScript website using Vite. Saved evidence and structured sample records support the findings, product comparison, and scoring examples. Browser state holds local selections and drafts; CSV and JSON exports make that work inspectable.

The quote, capacity, and alias controls run against the local sample. The website has no connection to DiaMedical’s internal catalog or analytics. Public observations, proposed changes, and calculated local results remain separate.
